title: Asia Pacific Women in Leadership Mentoring Program
content_markdown:
Extended Application Deadline: June 26, 2024 \| 4 PM \(extended for mentors only\)

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/documents/APWiL%20Mentoring%20Program%20-%20web%20image.jpg)

##### **\*\*UBC application deadline extended to June 26 \(mentors only\)\*\***

**Please note: This opportunity is primarily for faculty members; senior administrators can also apply as mentors\.**

[The APWiL Mentoring Program](https://apru.org/event/5th-cohort-apwil-mentoring-program/) \(APWiL\) provides international and intercultural opportunities for the empowerment, professional growth and development of aspiring women leaders within the member institutions of the Association of Pacific Rim Universities \(APRU\)\.

UBC is a proud member of APRU, a network of leading universities in the Asia Pacific region\. Sixty leading research universities from around the Pacific Rim are members, including more than 200,000 academic staff and two million students\.

### Mentees, are you an aspiring woman leader at UBC?

A year\-long program will match you with a mentor to help you:

-   Advance professional growth and leadership skills
-   Develop a self\-reflective understanding and acceptance of your personal leadership style and strengths, plus gain confidence in your unique abilities as a leader
-   Expand leadership acumen skills through training and learning from highly successful professionals outside their direct sphere of activity
-   Build a strong and supportive network from universities across the Asia Pacific
-   Gain insights and guidance to better tackle issues or challenges in the workplace

### Eligibility

1.  UBCV and UBCO faculty member \(academic appointment with at least five years and a maximum of seven years experience\)
2.  Identify as a woman \(cisgender, transgender, gender expansive and intersex people who identify as women\) or an individual of different gender identification who supports and is committed to the program mission
3.  Able to commit to a year\-long program \(September 2024\-October 2025\)

[More details](http://apru.org/event/5th-cohort-apwil-mentoring-program/)

### How to apply as a mentee

Include in your application: 

1.  Professional bio \(250 words\) with your full name, title, institution name and email 
2.  Statement of interest \(500 words\):
    -   Why would you like to participate in the program?  
    -   What do you hope to learn from your mentor?  
    -   What are one or two goals you would like to accomplish during your participation in the program? 
    -   Which topics would you like to discuss with your mentor?  

**Vancouver faculty**: Send your application package to [daniella\.weber@ubc\.ca](mailto:daniella.weber@ubc.ca) by June 5, 2024 at 4 pm PDT \(in the subject of your email, note that you are applying as a mentee\)\. 

### Mentors, are you an experienced leader looking to empower the next generation of women leaders?

-   Join a network of like\-minded professionals striving to drive gender balance in leadership positions at their universities\!
-   Advance leadership, coaching and mentoring skills of aspiring women leaders
-   Build a strong and supportive network from across the leading research universities of the Asia Pacific
-   Give back to the community in a meaningful way\.

### Eligibility

1.  UBCV and UBCO academic or administrative senior leaders \(at least 10 years experience\)
2.  Mentors of any gender are welcome to participate
3.  Able to commit to a year\-long program \(September 2024\-October 2025\)

[More details](http://apru.org/event/5th-cohort-apwil-mentoring-program/)

### How to apply as a mentor

Include in your application: 

1.  Professional bio \(250 words\) with your full name, title, institution name and email 
2.  Statement of interest \(500 words\): 
    -   Why would you like to participate in the program? 
    -   What do you aim to contribute to the program? Include any relevant mentoring and leadership experiences, as well as areas of expertise \(administrative and academic\) relevant to a mentee as it pertains to professional development 

**Vancouver faculty and administrators**: Send your application package to [daniella\.weber@ubc\.ca](mailto:daniella.weber@ubc.ca) by June 26, 2024 at 4 pm PDT \(in the subject of your email, note that you are applying as a mentor\)\. 

### What happens after I submit my application?

#### Selection process

Selecting representatives is an adjudication team from the Office of Global Engagement \(UBCV\), the Okanagan Campus International Office, and the Equity and Inclusion Office, sponsors of UBC’s participation this year\. The team will consider representation from both campuses, along with the candidates’ Statements of Interest\.

We will notify selected mentees by June 12, 2024\. Mentors will be notifed by June 28, 2024\.

The team will select up to two mentors \(senior academic or administrative leaders\) and two mentees \(aspiring women leaders\) to participate in the APRU Pacific Women in Leadership Mentoring Program 2025\. Please note: UBC must nominate the same number of mentors as mentees in order to ensure everyone in the program is matched\. Selected participants will be matched with a mentor/mentee from one of the 21 participating APRU member institutions\.

#### Timeline

-   June 5: UBC application deadline \(mentees\)
-   June 26: UBC application deadline \(mentors\)
-   July 10: Nominations sent to APRU
-   September 24: Program orientation
-   Week of September 30: Announcement of mentorship pairs

---

### Why join the mentoring program?

##### Benefits

-   Join a cohort of like\-minded professionals striving to drive gender balance in leadership positions at their university\.
-   Build a strong and supportive network from across the leading research universities of the Pacific Rim\.
-   Develop a supportive one\-on\-one mentoring relationship with a mentor/mentee\.
-   Mentors give back to the community in a meaningful way through supporting women in early career stages and developing their leadership skills\.
-   Mentors help empower the next generation of women leaders at their institution and across the region\.
-   Mentees advance their professional growth and leadership skills\.
-   Mentees expand their leadership acumen skills through training and learning from highly successful professionals outside their direct sphere of activity\.

##### What’s included:

-   One\-on\-one mentor\-mentee sessions
-   Virtual orientation kick\-off and graduation ceremony
-   Virtual workshops and seminars offering resource sharing, professional training and international exchange
-   Informal networking opportunities
-   Resource library
-   Optional in\-person summit

##### Testimonials from past participants:

### APWiL Mentor

Dr\. Samia Khan, Faculty Associate, Institute of Resources, Environment, and Sustainability \(IRES\), UBC Faculty of Science and Department of Curriculum and Pedagogy, UBC Faculty of Education:

*“The APWiL program has been a wonderful way for me to mentor a mid\-career faculty member at another university around the world\. Being a member of APRU also allowed me to participate in many virtual events on women in higher education leadership\.*

*My mentee and I shared an interest in research and academic leadership that crosses geographic boundaries with her work in Oceania and Asia and my research in the ASEAN \(Association of Southeast Asian Nations\) member countries and Africa\. We learned from one another and talked regularly about how to sustain international research teams\. Later, my mentee joined one my international research team meetings\.*

*Through her leadership and effort, I got an opportunity to travel to Australia on a subsequent study leave and be hosted by her national association to share my work on international collaboration and leadership experience with more than 20 universities in and beyond the Pacific Rim\. It was a tremendous highlight and our mentor\-mentee relationship continues: We will both be meeting again at the APWiL in\-person Summit, years after our cohort began\.”*

### APWiL Mentee

Dr\. Carla T\. Hilario, Assistant Professor, UBC Okanagan School of Nursing, Faculty of Health and Social Development:

*“The APWiL program has given me a valuable opportunity to grow my academic network across the Pacific Rim, build leadership and research capacity, and, most importantly, learn from my mentor\. Strategies such as mentorship agreements gave me guidance and structure to my experience\. I was recently selected to attend the inaugural APWiL Summit at Waipapa Taumata Rau University of Auckland, and am thrilled to be meeting other representatives in person, including my mentor\.”*

Read more [testimonials](https://apru.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/APWiL-3rd-Cohort-Alumni.pdf)\.

title: Prospective students
content_markdown:
Your program, projects, and contacts at UBC depend on whether you plan to come to UBC to do research and earn a salary as an employee or whether the research is part of your educational program as a student at your home institution\.  

VIRS is the approved program for international students who want to engage in full\-time research at UBC under the supervision of UBC faculty member\. If you meet the [eligibility requirements](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/node/3751) and do not wish to take courses at UBC, consider [**applying to the VIRS program**](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/visiting-international-research-students/how-apply "How to apply")***\.***

For students interested in also taking coursework or receiving compensation for research, consider other UBC options outlined here:

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/documents/GG%20VIRS%20flow.jpeg)

**Helpful acronyms** 

-   **LMIA:** Labour Market Impact Assessment
-   **IRCC:** Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, formerly known as Citizenship and Immigration Canada 

##### Information for non\-VIRS options: 

-   **International Undergraduate \(bachelor's\) students**  
    -   Taking courses and doing research: [Visiting Students \(VISI\) through Non\-Degree Studies](https://students.ubc.ca/enrolment/courses/non-degree-studies/non-degree-studies-visiting)   
         
-   **International Graduate \(master's or PhD\) students**
    -   Taking course and/or doing research: [Visiting International Students \(VISI\) through Graduate Studies](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/prospective-students/application-admission/visitors-international-universities)—see “Other Visiting Students”   
         
-   **Canadian Citizens/Permanent Resident, Graduate \(master's or PhD\) students**  
    -   Taking course and/or doing research: [Visiting Students \(VISI\) through Graduate Studies](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/prospective-students/application-admission/visitors-canadian-universities)     
         
-   **Non\-students**
    -   Research\-only, salaried: Contact the Human Resources team within the hosting academic department—see [Faculty Relations](https://hr.ubc.ca/contact/contact-faculty-relations-and-academic-leadership-program-aldp)

##### Finding a UBC supervisor as a VIRS student 

As a student applicant, it's your responsibility to identify, contact and get approval from a UBC faculty member who will be your VIRS supervisor\. Identify a potential supervisor who best matches your research interests and academic background\. 

UBC's Faculty of Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies website hosts a [database of UBC professors](https://www.grad.ubc.ca/virs/hosts) and their research interests, and lists which are available to host VIRS students\. 

Search through faculties offered at UBC to help identify your potential supervisor\. 

-   [UBC Vancouver faculties](https://www.ubc.ca/our-campuses/vancouver/directories/faculties-schools.html)
-   [UBC Okanagan faculties](https://ok.ubc.ca/academics/faculties-and-schools/)

##### Joint Doctoral Research Scholar Designation 

If you are a VIRS applicant who is registered in a PhD program at a recognized institution, you might be eligible for the Joint Doctoral Research Scholar designation\. To qualify, students must: 

-   Be registered in a PhD program at a recognized institution or at UBC
-   Be registered at UBC as a Visiting Graduate Student or Visiting International Research Student, if not already a registered PhD student at UBC
-   Have faculty co\-supervisors of their doctoral research program at each university, which are formally approved by the appropriate individual/office at each university 

Joint Doctoral Research Scholars will be eligible to obtain a confirmation letter from Graduate and Postdoctoral Studies to validate that their doctoral thesis research was co\-supervised by a UBC faculty member and that they attended UBC as a Joint Doctoral Research Scholar as part of their doctoral studies at another university\. [Read more](http://vancouver.calendar.ubc.ca/faculties-colleges-and-schools/faculty-graduate-and-postdoctoral-studies/academic-regulations/joint-doctoral-research-scholars)\.

To be considered: 

1.  Check if you are [eligible for VIRS](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/visiting-international-research-students/eligibility-requirements "Eligibility requirements")
2.  Complete the [JDRS request form](https://global.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/documents/JDRS_form_Dec-6-22.pdf)
3.  [Apply for VIRS](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/visiting-international-research-students/how-apply "How to apply") and upload your completed JDRS request form to your application

[Check eligibility](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/node/3751)

title: Université de Lausanne - SUR Program
content_markdown:
## About

### About the programs

**Program dates:** 8 weeks from July to August

The SUR Programme at Université de Lausanne hosts about 20 students from around the world to perform cutting\-edge research projects within one of the host laboratories of the UNIL Faculty of Biology and Medicine\. Students spend time in a laboratory setting, engaging with faculty members on research topics as well as academic activities\. Students have the opportunity to attend career guidance workshops in academia and take part in a number of social and cultural activities\. At the end of the summer, students present the results of their research on a poster during a joint UNIL/EPFL Symposium and write a final report\.

**Research Area:** Biology and Medical Sciences

[See program details](https://www.unil.ch/eb-sur/en/home.html)

## Eligibility requirements

### General Research Abroad eligibility

-   You must have at least a 70% average in your most recent academic term of full\-time studies prior to application\. We are looking at your Term 1 \(Fall term\) grades for summer research abroad experiences
-   You should have full\-time student status as defined by your faculty in the year prior to your research abroad experience
-   You need to be a UBC student in good standing \(e\.g\., not be under academic or non\-academic discipline\)
-   You must maintain a 70% average prior to your exchange departure

### Program\-specific eligibility

-   Be a 3rd or 4th year student by the time the program begins in a relevant discipline\.
-   Students must be returning for a semester of study following the program\.
-   Given the competitive nature of the program Go Global encourages students with an average of 80% or higher to apply\.
-   Meet any additional lab project requirements as outlined on the program website\.

## Accessibility 

If you are considering applying for a Go Global program and you identify as having a [disability](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/disability-accommodation-policy/) or pre\-existing health condition, you are encouraged to discuss any disability\-related barriers with The Centre for Accessibility to enhance your full participation in the program\.

The [Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility) \(Vancouver\) 604 822\-5844  

[Disability Resource Centre](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/academic-success/disability-resources/) \(Okanagan\) 250 807\-8053 

## Transfer credit 

UBC does not recognize credit for research abroad programs and does not grant transfer credit for these experiences\. If a partner university offers credit for your Research Abroad program, save the transcript or certificate of completion for your future records\. 

## How to apply

After you submit your application to Go Global, you will be contacted by the advisor with instructions on the next steps for applying directly to your program\(s\) of choice\.

### 1\. Apply to Go Global once you’ve identified programs you're interested in

-   Submit your Go Global application [online](https://ubc-horizons.symplicity.com/student)\. You can apply for up to 3 programs on one application\.
-   Go Global will contact you with instructions on how to apply to the partner and an electronic copy of your UBC transcript\.

### 2\. Apply directly to the partner university

-   Each research program will have detailed instructions on how to apply and strict submission deadlines\.
-   All research programs will need supporting documents that typically include:
    -   Academic references \(1 – 3\)
    -   Letter of intent
    -   Curriculum vitae
    -   UBC transcript

## Application deadline

[December 10, 2025](https://ubc-horizons.symplicity.com/student)

## Program costs and fees

In addition to paying the Go Global fee following the Go Global deadline, students are responsible for the cost of travel and living associated with participating in this program\.

Housing is provided for students participating in this program and is coordinated and paid for by the SUR program\.

## Funding for Research Abroad

### **Go Global Research Abroad Award**

$1,000 per research experience

### Eligibility requirements

All students accepted into a research abroad program, through Go Global, will be considered for this award\. A separate application is not required\. If you meet the eligibility criteria, then you will be notified of your award near the start of the summer term\.

To be eligible for the award, you must have an average of at least 70% on your best 24 credits in the Winter Session of the previous year \(with no failed or incomplete courses\)\.

If you were on a co\-op work term, you must have at least 70% on your best 12 credits in the other term\. 

You will be automatically considered for the award, so you will not need to apply separately\.

### Partner University Funding

Accepted participants are eligible for a scholarship of up to 1,500 Swiss Francs \(roughly $1800 CAD\) for living expenses\. Students will be responsible for additional living and travel expenses\.  Housing is arranged and paid for by the program\. 

Students may be eligible for funds to cover travel expenses to Lausanne of up to $1,200 Swiss Francs \(roughly $1,500 CAD\) for international travel\.

## Go Global fee and withdrawal policy

The Go Global Fee \($431\.50\) is an administrative fee required for all applicants to all Go Global programs\. The fee will be posted to your Workday account 1\-3 weeks following your acceptance to the partner program, and will be due approximately 2 weeks later\. You will be notified of the due date by email once the fee is posted\. The fee is **non\-refundable**\. However, it may be adjusted if you withdraw from your Research Abroad experience\.

#### **If you withdraw from Go Global**

To withdraw from your Go Global Research Abroad program, you must contact Go Global to request a withdrawal\. You will then be asked to complete a short withdrawal form\.

Students who withdraw from a Go Global Research Abroad Program by March 30th will have their Go Global fee adjusted to $335\.00 \(a refund of $96\.50\)\.

If you have questions or would like to request a withdrawal, please connect with your Go Global advisor or contact Go Global [here](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5no0NEltKbm0yY6)\. 

## Pre\-Departure policy

UBC is committed to preparing students for safe and successful international experiences\. In order to achieve this, any student participating in a Go Global Program must complete the following:

-   All [UBC Student Safety Abroad](https://safetyabroad.ubc.ca/) requirements
-   Go Global Program\-specific pre\-departure requirements 

Failure to successfully complete these and any other requirements may result in withdrawal from the Go Global Program\.

## Contact Go Global

[SUBMIT YOUR QUESTIONS HERE](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5no0NEltKbm0yY6%20%C2%A0) 

### In\-person and Virtual Drop\-in advising hours

If you need to book an advising appointment, please complete the [online request form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3EEmkwnTWtrG04Z)\. Appointments will be held through Zoom or by phone, and can be scheduled between **8:30 am and 4:30 pm PT** from **Monday to Friday\.** 

If you require an appointment outside of these hours, contact Go Global and they will do their best to accommodate\. Appointments outside of regular hours can only be accommodated virtually\.

\-\->

-   **Tuesday:** 1:00 \- 3:00 pm
-   **Wednesday:** 1:00 \- 3:00 pm

title: VIRS: Supervisor FAQs
content_markdown:
##### \[Supervisors\] Why does the VIRS pathway exist?

VIRS is the senate\-approved pathway for all international students that are visiting UBC for research purposes \(unless  formally appointed as staff through Human Resources and will be obtaining a work permit\)\. The pathway was created to offer a consistent status and set of support resources for faculty and their visiting research students, and to avoid risks associated with being on campus without formal affiliation\.

VIRS students are admitted to the university with [full\-time student status](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/ubc-definitions-immigration-purposes#full-time) for the period of the research studies\. They obtain a university student number, online login and UBC student Card\. The Login ID and the UBC Card are used to access our Libraries and related systems, online research tools, and may be used to access certain physical locations on campus \(labs, computer labs, departmental lounges, etc\)\.

VIRS students are also invited to an orientation meeting and some social events where they meet other VIRS students that are on campus\.

title: Paris - Field Study in Nineteenth-Century Art - ARTH 439 (3 credits)
content_markdown:
- **Row 1**

- **Row 2**

    This course is led by [**Jillian Lerner**](https://ahva.ubc.ca/profile/jillian-lerner/) **&** [**Nikki Georgopulos**](https://ahva.ubc.ca/profile/nicole-georgopulos/)**, Faculty of Arts**
    
    -   **Course dates**: May 12, 2025 \- June 20, 2025
    -   **Travel dates**:  May 20, 2025 \- June 5, 2025 \(tentative\)

    -   **Locations visited**: Paris \(France\)

    -   Funding available \(click through to learn more about each award\) 
        -   [Go Global Award](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/awards-students-participating-go-global)
        -   **Faculty of Arts Cultural Exchange in France Grant \(CEFG\)**: see below under "Program fees and costs\."
        -   [Global Pathfinder Award](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/awards-students-participating-go-global) \(non\-Arts students may apply for this program\)
            -   Note: Recipients of this award will not qualify for the $1000 Go Global Award\.

    Application instructions [here](http://global.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/global-seminars/preparing-apply)\.
    
    [Apply](http://ubc-horizons.symplicity.com/student)

##### About the course

This immersive summer course takes students to study nineteenth\-century visual culture in the museums and built environment of Paris\. Offered in English, this hybrid seminar will combine online preparation with two weeks of intensive field study in Paris\. To lay the thematic and methodological foundations for study abroad, the course will begin with one week of remote engagement with recorded lectures, readings, and zoom seminars\. Participants will then convene in Paris for two weeks of experiential learning centered on museum visits, workshops, walking tours, and research in French collections\. Subsequently, students will have another two weeks to complete their assignments; they may choose to continue traveling or return home as the remaining coursework can be done independently and submitted online\.

Our exploration of nineteenth\-century art and cultural history will focus on changing patterns of spectatorship, visual attraction, and display\. Visits to Parisian museums, archives, and historical sites will enable first\-hand examination of photography, print, painting, sculpture, decorative arts, waxworks, and displays of mechanical ingenuity\. Evaluating histories of colonization, capitalist spectacle, and visions of Paris as the "capital of modernity," we will also consider critical and creative practices of resistance and repair\. We will interrogate imperialist claims and elite privileges, observing how these are manifest in past and present visual practices, cityscapes, and rituals of art tourism\. 

-   **May 12 \- 20:** There will be a few course meetings scheduled on Zoom\. 
-   **May 20 \- June 5:** Paris dates
-   **June 5 \- June 20:** Time to complete and submit assignments\. 

##### Program eligibility  

###### **General Global Seminar requirements**

To participate in a Global Seminar, students must: 

-   Be in good standing in their faculty \(as defined by home faculty\)  
-   In the year leading up to the Global Seminar, have full\-time student status \(as defined by home faculty\)    
-   Have completed 2nd year requirements before the start of the program \(i\.e\. 3rd or 4th year standing\)  
-   Have at least a 70% academic average in your last full\-time academic session before applying    
-   Maintain a 70% academic average leading up to the program  
-   Meet any program\-specific requirements listed below including pre\-requisites before participating 

###### **Program Specific requirements**

-   3 credits of ARTH strongly encouraged\. ARTH majors will be given priority\. 

**Final selection will be made by the lead faculty program directors\. Space in the program may be limited\.** 

Graduating students registered full\-time \(min 9 credits in most faculties\) in Term 2 may participate in a Global Seminar as an Unclassified student in the summer\. During the selection process, preference may be given to students returning to UBC in Term 1\.

##### Experience and conditions in the Field

The learning environment will be variable, ranging from museums and archives to parks, markets, and streets\. Our itinerary will involve a lot of walking, standing on hard surfaces, navigating crowded urban spaces, and riding public transportation \(mostly an underground subway system\)\. These conditions favour able\-bodied students who do not have difficulties with mobility or agoraphobia\. The teaching team is eager to partner with prospective students to identify needs and provide extra support, resources, alternatives, or flexibility that would reduce barriers to participation\.  

Regrettably, many of the Parian sites and cultural institutions we will visit, and the Paris metro system, are not wheel\-chair accessible, which constrains our ability to accommodate related accessibility needs\.

Participants do not need French language competency to participate in the course; we will provide instruction in English, and bilingual members of the cohort will support necessary communications\. 

##### Accommodations

Hostel\-style accommodation while abroad\. Students should expect to share rooms with 1, 2 or more students\. 

##### Program fees, costs, and funding

###### **Approximate fees:** $4000

\*The final fee depends on the number of students in the seminar\. All Global Seminars only run if there is a minimum number of students enrolled\.  

###### **Program fees include:**

-   Accommodations \(lodging during the travel portion of the program\)  
-   Program\- related travel in\-country; \(e\.g\. buses\)  
-   Excursions and entrance fees  
-   Some group meals  
-   On\-site guest lectures
-   Go Global Fee 

Note that students may occasionally be asked to take private or public transport to\-and\-from program activities at their own cost \(e\.g\. local buses, metros/subways, taxis/ride\-shares in urban areas\.\)

###### **Not Included:**  

-   Flights 
-   UBC tuition for credits   
-   Visa/country entrance fees   
-   Health or travel insurance  
-   Most meals 
-   Personal spending money\*   

\* Some examples of personal costs included: mobile communication, personal transportation that is not related to the learning outcomes of the program, additional meals that are not already identified as part of the Program Fee, immunizations, Visas, etc\.  

##### Cultural Experience in France Grant \(CEFG\) for Arts students

This program is generously supported by the Cultural Experience in France Grant for Arts students\. Eligible Arts students applying to the program will automatically be considered for the CEFG funding\. No additional application is required\.

Students who have previously received large awards for a Go Global program \(like GSO, ARA, Pathfinder or others\) may participate in this program and be eligible for ARA or CEFG funding\. However, students who have not received major Go Global Awards will be prioritized for funded spaces\. There is a limited number of fully funded spots available in this program\. 

|  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | **Full CEFG Funding** | **Partial CEFG Funding** | **Non\-Arts students** |
| Program Fees \(inclusive of Go Global fee\) | $0 | $1500 | $4000 |
| Award | $1800 | $1000 | $1000 |

---

 **Eligibility Criteria:**

-   Acceptance into this program\.
-   Enrolled in a UBC Vancouver degree program in the Faculty of Arts \(B\.A\., B\.Mus\., etc\)\.
-   Have a minimum GPA of 70% in the top 24 credits of the previous academic year with no failed or incomplete courses in the assessed period\.
-   Current full\-time students \(min 9 credits per term\) in 2024\-25 Academic Year
-   Depending on the number of eligible candidates, priority may be given to students in a French major or minor\.

To be eligible for the 100% funding, there is one ***additional*** consideration:

-   Demonstration of financial need
    -   Priority will be given to students who meet the eligibility criteria for financial aid \(which includes receiving non\-repayable loans and bursaries\), as defined and determined by UBC Enrolment Services\.
    -   Other students will have the opportunity to provide a written statement and budget to demonstrate their unmet financial needs\.

Students accepted into this program who are not eligible for the Cultural Experience in France Grant will receive a $1,000 Go Global Award\.

[Back to All Global Seminar Programs](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/global-seminars/programs "Global Seminar Programs")

### Program Safety

All travel and program activities involve risk of harm to participants\. Go Global and Seminar program leads take reasonable precautions to reduce risks\. However, not all harms can be anticipated or prevented\. 

While travelling on UBC programs, students have a responsibility for their own safety and the safety of the group\.

Some common issues for travellers include:

-   Illness and injuries \(e\.g\. respiratory illnesses, flu, food poisoning, sprained ankles, etc\.\)
-   Fatigue and heat exhaustion
-   Violence like robbery, or gender\- and race\-based harassment or attacks, especially in urban areas
-   Traffic accidents
-   Lost documents \(passports, credit cards, etc\.\)

**Before Applying:**

-   Get to know the places you will be travelling by using available resources like [Global Affairs Canada travel reports](https://travel.gc.ca/travelling/advisories)\.
-   Consider your own mental and physical health alongside what you know about the conditions during the program \(e\.g\. how physical is the program? What are the living conditions? What can I do to prepare myself?\)

**Before departure:**  

-   Participate in all pre\-departure activities offered by Go Global and your program teaching team to learn about the program and ways to prevent and respond to incidents\.
-   Ensure you have adequate travel medical insurance that will cover you in the location and for the duration of your trip\.
-   Be aware of how to use your travel medical insurance, if you need it, and where to access medical care or other emergency assistance in the locations where you will be travelling\. 

**During the program:** 

-   If you don’t feel safe, say something\! Let your program leads know how you feel, or about incidents that occur\. Don’t hesitate to contact Go Global during your program\. 
-   Know your own needs: be aware of your own mental and physical health and your limits\. Communicate with your program lead and group about making adjustments, as needed\. 

#### **Public health: COVID\-19 and other diseases**

Students and faculty are required to comply with the entry requirements of the host country, regulations of transportation carriers, and any local public health orders\. These rules might require vaccinations \(e\.g\. for COVID\-19, yellow fever, etc\.\) to enter the country or to participate in certain program activities\. Some places may require masking, testing or isolation in various circumstances\. It is your responsibility to research and comply with any requirements\.

COVID\-19 and other infections can spread easily in a group setting\. Most programs involve shared accommodations\. Unless required by local public health authorities, isolation for those infected during the program may not be possible\.   
   
Review local requirements before applying and before departure\. Check the [Global Affairs Canada Advisory](https://travel.gc.ca/travelling/advisories) under Entry Requirements for your Global Seminar destination to learn more\. Keep in mind that program conditions can vary and rules can change before or during your trip\.

title: Global Insider: Exploring Culture, Coastlines, and Campus Life in Australia
content_markdown:
UBC graduate Emma Martin\-Rousselle shares how an exchange at UNSW in Sydney sparked spontaneity, global exploration, and a deeper sense of academic and personal growth\.

January 14, 2026

*Are you a UBC undergrad thinking about going on a student exchange? It can be a daunting decision\. You might wonder, what's it like spending a year or a semester in another country? How can you prepare? And how do you handle it when things go sideways? We talked with a group of* [*UBC Global Ambassadors*](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/new-student-experiences/global-ambassadors-and-global-cultural-ambassadors) *who studied abroad with a* [*Go Global program*](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global)*\. They spoke with us candidly, sharing their personal impressions, fears and misgivings, best memories, top tips and advice\. \(This story is part of a series of Global Exchange Insider interviews\.\)* 

*Meet Emma Martin\-Rousselle, a recent UBC B\+MM graduate\. She completed her M\.M\. dual\-degree in December 2025 and B\.A\. Sociology in May 2025\. She is originally from Deep River, ON, Canada\.*

It was 7am in Sydney, Australia, and I had just gotten off one of the longest flights I had ever taken in my life\. After finishing my summer internship Friday, packing up Saturday, and sharing tearful goodbyes, I boarded my flight to head to exchange\. Then, following a day of travel \(including a Hong Kong layover adventure\), I finally made it to Sydney\!

Jet lagged, I got into a taxi and, after arriving at my accommodation, dropped my bags and slept for a few hours\. When I woke up, I met my new housemates, who quickly convinced me to join their trip to Cairns the next week\. Eleven of them were planning to spend the week snorkeling or scuba diving in the Great Barrier Reef and exploring the Daintree Rainforest\. That same day I arrived in Sydney, I booked my flights, along with a spot in a scuba diving certification course, so I could join a few roommates on an overnight scuba tour to the reef\.

This type of spontaneity is exactly what I wanted to achieve in my exchange\. After a busy three years of university, I hoped this would be a chance to explore the world – even though I’d be studying at [UNSW](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/exchange/university-new-south-wales "University of New South Wales"), I knew there’d also be many opportunities to check items off my bucket list\. With my new roommates, I travelled across New Zealand, hiked the Blue Mountains\. I even met up with one of my roommates in Vietnam over Christmas to ride the Ha Giang Loop\. I also travelled solo for the first time, learning to surf, exploring new places, and meeting incredible people along the way\.

So, here’s a bit about my exchange experience: before, during, and after\!

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo3_EmmaMR%20%281%29.jpeg)

*Overlooking Fitzroy Falls in Morton National Park, Australia \(photo: Emma Martin\-Rousselle\)*

#### Before you go   

**Why did you pick the** [**University of New South Wales**](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/exchange/university-new-south-wales "University of New South Wales") **for your exchange? How did you hear about it?**    
I knew I wanted to go to Australia for my exchange: it was a far\-away place I had never been to before and I wasn’t sure if I’d ever have the opportunity to visit there long\-term other than doing an exchange\. There were a lot of things that appealed to me about Australia, such as the beautiful nature, the beaches and the cultural similarities to Canada\. UNSW was my top choice because of its trimester system\. Most Australian universities have their spring term from July \- November, but UNSW’s third trimester runs from September \- November, matching with UBC Term 1\. I personally needed a university whose term dates aligned with UBC so I could complete a summer internship and still graduate on time\.

**What was the application process like? Any tips?**   
The application process was straightforward: GoGlobal helped make the process very easy\! The only thing I had to submit to UNSW was an official transcript with my final grades, which GoGlobal provided\. Course registration was a bit different from UBC’s: we first selected our classes and then, after approval of those courses by UNSW admin, could select our timetable\.

**How did you prepare? Anything to be aware of? \(travel, cultural differences, classes, etc\.\)**   
One thing that students interested in UNSW should be aware of is the housing situation\. When I went to UNSW, most exchange students were not eligible to live in [on\-campus residence\.](https://www.unsw.edu.au/accommodation) This required us to find our own housing off\-campus, usually only after arriving in Sydney\. Personally, I found housing through a privately operated company that caters specifically to exchange students\. They also allowed me to sign my lease before I got to Sydney\. I had a good experience living with others studying abroad and my roommate was a fellow UBC student who I met at a pre\-departure mixer event\! However, housing through this private company was really overpriced compared to other options\. 

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo%205_EmmaMR_0.jpeg)

*Emma \(right\) with her partner, Will, at Newcastle Beach, Australia \(photo: Emma Martin\-Rousselle\)*

**What worries did you have beforehand? How did you overcome the anxiety?**  
I was lucky that, going into the experience, this wasn’t my first exchange – I did a high school exchange in France and, with that experience, knew what it was like to pick up and move to a new country\. That said, moving didn’t feel any less daunting\. I still worried about making friends, academics, and the long trip\. I overcame my anxiety by speaking to friends who had had similar experiences\. Before exchange, I reconnected with Australian friends who I met on my high school exchange, and I also spoke  to previous GoGlobal students who went to Australia\. I found it helpful to hear about their experiences\. I also connected with my housemates and roommate on social media before arriving, to help ease some of the pressure about living with new people, and was really glad to have done so\!

#### During the experience

**How was the overall experience? What did you learn?**   
I loved Australia: the weather, the travel opportunities, the lifestyle\. I enjoyed my experience so much that I hope to move back to Australia in the next few years; and, I learned how much I thrive in the Australian lifestyle and sunny weather\!

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo1_EmmaMR.jpeg)

*Cape Tribulation near Cairns, Australia \- one of the few places in the world where two world heritage sites meet\! \(photo: Emma Martin\-Rousselle\)*

**If you could change something or do it differently, what would you change or do?**   
I wish I’d explored Sydney more instead of focusing on weekend trips or my routine in my neighbourhood\. I often forgot that I could spend my weekend travelling around Sydney, too, since it’s such a big city\! I returned to Australia six months after my exchange ended and had time to explore Sydney a bit more, and that’s what made me realize I missed out on so much during my exchange\.

**How were the academics?**   
UNSW felt similar to UBC, if not more relaxed\. I took all electives and, because of the trimester layout, only took 3 courses \(worth 12 UBC credits\)\. All of my lectures were recorded, so most students \- even non\-exchange students \- seemed to only attend the mandatory tutorials, and I only went to campus a couple of days a week\. I also took courses that I felt I wouldn’t have been able to take at UBC: Media in the Asia\-Pacific; Sydney History, Landscapes and People; and Migrants and Refugees in Australia and the World\. These courses gave me a new and unique perspective on the world\.

**How was the social aspect?**  
As mentioned above, I had a great social life because of my roommates, as well as local friends I met\. Travel was a huge part of my exchange, including a six\-week backpacking trip I took at the end of my exchange, and 10 days spent in New Zealand over my reading week\. I also hiked the Blue Mountains, went camping, celebrated the AFL Grand Final in Melbourne, and even attended an opera at the Sydney Opera House\. I honestly made so many great memories\.

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo2_EmmaMR.jpeg)

*Sydney Opera House in Sydney, Australia \(photo: Emma Martin\-Rousselle\)*

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo%204_EmmaMR_0.jpeg)

*Emma \(left\) with a friend, Sidnee \(right\), on the Great Ocean Road near Geelong, Australia \(photo: Emma Martin\-Rousselle\)*

#### After the experience

**Would you recommend this experience to others? What can they look forward to?**   
Absolutely yes\! Australia is an amazing country and there are so many things to look forward to\. Sydney offers vibrant city life, culture, and beaches, plus endless opportunities to travel around nearby regions and enjoy hiking and the outdoors \- it’s very similar to Vancouver, but with nicer weather year\-round\. Though you might be less likely to explore neighboring countries compared to going on exchange to Europe or Asia, I still got to travel to five countries in Asia, as well as seeing New Zealand and three states of Australia\. I also could have seen so much more of Australia, and definitely want to go back to see other parts of the country I missed\.

**What was the impact on your academic and personal development?**    
I wanted to see if I could picture myself living and working in Australia in the future, and, after my exchange, the answer is yes\! The experience also made me more spontaneous, learning to say ‘yes’ to opportunities from impromptu group trips to solo travel, and has inspired me to hopefully do more backpacking/solo travel in the future\.

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo6_EmmaMR%20%282%29_0.jpeg)

 *Hobbiton movie set near Auckland, New Zealand \(photo: Emma Martin\-Rousselle\)*

**Read more Go Global** [**student stories**](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/student-experiences/student-stories)**\.** 

---

## Who can go?

-   All students who have a minimum cumulative average of 73% or above may attend this partnership

## Academic planning

### Term dates

-   UBC Term 1 \(DIS Semester 1\): Mid August to Mid December
-   UBC Term 2 \(DIS Semester 2\): Mid January to Mid May  

### Areas of study available:

-   Architecture and Landscape Architecture

-   Commerce \(UBCV\)
-   Education
-   Fine Arts
-   Health Sciences
-   Management \(UBCO\)
-   Science

### Course availability and restrictions

-   Programs in Arts, Business, Computer Science, Sustainability, Geographical Sciences, Education, Design, Neuroscience, Medieval Studies, Philosophy\. English, Urban Studies, Social Justice
-   Your program at DIS is determined by your choice of a "core course"
-   Core courses include a week\-long Program Study Tour to a European destination and a Core Course Week, comprised of a two\-day seminar on\-site, and three\-day short study tour within the country, or to a nearby destination\. See DIS website for more information on Program Study Tours and Core Course Week in Stockholm and Copenhagen
-   In addition to their core course, students register for "elective courses"

Students take 15 credits

title: Global Insider: History, Culture, and Exploration in Paris
content_markdown:
UBC student Ghita Adnane reflects on how her Global Seminar experience in Paris has inspired future career plans, a greater sense of global exploration, and transformative personal growth\.

May 14, 2026

*Are you a UBC undergrad thinking about going on a student exchange? It can be a daunting decision\. You might wonder, what's it like spending a year or a semester in another country? How can you prepare? And how do you handle it when things go sideways? We talked with a group of* [*UBC Global Ambassadors*](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/new-student-experiences/global-ambassadors-and-global-cultural-ambassadors) *who studied abroad with a* [*Go Global program*](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global)*\. They spoke with us candidly, sharing their personal impressions, fears and misgivings, best memories, top tips and advice\. \(This story is part of a series of Global Exchange Insider interviews\.\)* 

**Program Featured:** Paris, Capital of Modernity, HIST 390 taught by Dr\. Michael Lanthier, Department of History\.  
  
This program was generously funded by the Faculty of Arts Cultural Experience in France Grant thanks to an anonymous donor   
  
*Ghita Adnane is a 3\[rd\] year undergraduate student in the Urban Studies program in the Faculty of Arts\. She was born in Morocco and raised in Surrey, BC\.*  
 

[Musée d'Orsay during a class walking tour \(Photo Credits: Anonymous\)](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo%203_1.jpg)

*Musée d'Orsay during a class walking tour \(Photo Credit: Anonymous\)*

#### Before you go   

**Why did you pick** [**Paris: Capital of Modernity \(HIST 390\)**](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/ubc-student-programs/global-seminars/programs/paris-capital-modernity-hist-390-3-credits) **for your Global Seminar?** **How did you hear about it?**  
I have always wanted to live in Paris, ever since my one\-day layover trip there in 2024\. I fell in love with the city, and seeing the Eiffel Tower for the first time felt unreal and magical\. When I got to UBC, I learned about Go Global during Imagine Day—that’s when I found out about [Global Seminars](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/global-seminars)\. It stood out to me because it’s different from a traditional student exchange\. 

That fall, I started researching the [seminars available](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/global-seminars/programs), and Paris HIST 390 caught my attention because I was interested in the topic of modernity and how Paris transformed into the city we know today\.  

**What was the application process like? Any tips?**  
The application process was quite straightforward\. I applied during the Round 1 deadline in December 2024\. The application consisted of several written questions about your motivation and previous experiences traveling abroad or working in a team\. 

In January, I received an email inviting me to an interview with Professor Lanthier\. This was an opportunity to talk about why I wanted to participate in the global seminar and what I hoped to learn or gain from the experience\. The interview was conversational and included a few questions about group dynamics and previous international experiences\. 

One tip I would give is to research the seminar topics beforehand and connect them to your academic interests or experiences\. This helps show your genuine interest and engagement\. A few weeks later, I received my acceptance\.

**How did you prepare? Anything to be aware of?**   
I prepared by researching Paris extensively on social media\. Since it was my first time traveling abroad alone, I wanted to be ready for any situation\. It was also helpful to talk to people who had previously traveled there to get tips and recommendations\. This helped me plan what to pack based on the weather and safety considerations\. 

I recommend bringing good sneakers, since the lectures were all walking tours\. I averaged around 20,000 steps a day, so comfortable footwear is essential\. I also suggest bringing a fanny pack, water, and sun protection\. Be sure to check the weather before going, as it can be unpredictable\. Bring warm layers like jackets or hoodies, as it tends to get cold at night\.  
 

[Walking through the Gardens of Versailles \(Photo Credits: Ghita Adnane\)](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo%204_0.jpg)

*Walking through the Gardens of Versailles \(Photo Credit: Ghita Adnane\)*

**What worries did you have beforehand? How did you overcome anxiety?**  
Paris has a reputation for pickpocketing, so I was quite nervous about that, especially since it was my first time traveling alone\. I did a lot of research on ways to protect myself and prevent pickpocketing\. I bought a phone chain so I could keep my phone attached to my wrist, which helped me feel more secure\. I also used a fanny pack and a zippered shoulder bag to keep my belongings safe\. 

Thankfully, I didn’t have any negative experiences on the metro or while exploring the city\. I found Paris to be quite safe overall, but I would still recommend staying alert\. 

#### During the experience

**How was the overall experience? What did you learn?**   
My overall experience was amazing, I still think about my trip to this day\. It changed me for the better\. I learned a lot about myself and how independent I can be\. Although I was nervous about traveling alone, I ended up having an incredible time and felt safe throughout the trip\. 

I learned to be adaptable, open\-minded, and comfortable navigating a new environment\. I also learned a lot about the culture and felt very comfortable by the end of the three weeks\. The experience solidified my decision to move to Paris, and I’m now planning to do an exchange semester in France during Term 1 because I loved it so much\.  
 

[Antibes, France during a weekend trip from Paris\. \(Photo Credits: Ghita Adnane\)](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo%201_1.jpg)

*Antibes, France during a weekend trip from Paris \(Photo Credit: Ghita Adnane\)*

**If you could change something or do it differently, what would you change/do?**  
I would create a list of places I wanted to visit and things I wanted to try\. Paris is such a large city that it can feel overwhelming at times, and it’s impossible to do everything\. Having a plan and setting priorities before arriving would help make the most of your time, especially since three weeks go by quickly\. 

I wish I had done that, because there were times when I felt indecisive and ended up not doing much, which I regretted afterward\.

**How were the academics?**  
The academics were similar to a regular UBC course but more condensed and fast\-paced, like summer courses\. However, I really enjoyed the structure and assignments\. 

The course was very interactive\. It included a pre\-departure component in Vancouver, where we covered key topics and readings\. In Paris, the lectures were essentially walking tours in different parts of the city, depending on the topics we were studying\.  
 

[A group walking tour in Champs de Mars \(Photo Credits: Ghita Adnane\)](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo%205_1.jpg)

*A group walking tour in Champs de Mars \(Photo Credit: Ghita Adnane\)*

**How was the social aspect of the trip?**  
The social aspect was one of the highlights of the trip\. Since Global Seminars involve a group of UBC students, it was easy to connect with others\. We created a group chat before meeting together, which helped break the ice\. 

During the pre\-departure session, we met in person for the first time and quickly got along\. There were about 14 students, and many of us were roommates\. We cooked together, went on small trips, and explored the city as a group\. The walking tours also gave us plenty of time to bond and create lasting memories\. 

One of the best parts of Global Seminars is the friendships you build as they often continue even after returning to UBC\.

#### After the experience

**Would you recommend this experience to other students? What can they look forward to?**  
I would definitely recommend doing a Global Seminar at least once during your undergraduate degree\. It’s a unique opportunity that you won’t have after graduation\. Not only do you get to explore a new city, but the experience also counts toward your degree\. 

It was the highlight of my undergrad\. I learned so much about myself, experienced Paris in a meaningful way, and made friendships and memories that I will always cherish\.   
 

[View from the Galeries Lafayette Champs\-Élysées \(Photo Credits: Ghita Adnane\)](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo%202_3.jpg)

*View from the Galeries Lafayette Champs\-Élysées \(Photo Credit: Ghita Adnane\)*  

**What was the impact on your academic and personal development?**  
Academically, I gained a deeper understanding of Paris’s history through walking tours, museums, and lectures\. It was incredible to see history come to life in front of me\. The hands\-on learning experience is something you don’t get in a traditional classroom\. The walking tours also allowed us to explore parts of Paris we might not have seen otherwise, especially with guidance from the professor\. It changed the way I viewed the city and added depth to my understanding of it\. 

On a personal level, this was my first time traveling alone for an extended period\. I did feel homesick during the first few days, but I gradually adapted to the new environment with the support of my peers\. I also tried solo travel for the first time, which helped build my confidence and independence\. Overall, I learned a lot about myself and pushed outside of my comfort zone by trying new things\.  
 

[A visit to the Grand Mosque of Paris for a weekly assignment \(Photo Credit: Ghita Adnane\)](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Photo%206_1.jpg)

*A visit to the Grand Mosque of Paris for a weekly assignment \(Photo Credit: Ghita Adnane\)*

[Apply](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/node/3658)

## About the program

Aarhus University \(AU\) is an excellent choice for students interested in studying in Scandinavia\. Located in the city of Aarhus \(just 3 hrs from Copenhagen\), AU Summer University offers over 85 courses in a breadth of areas including STEM, Management, Law, Economics, Health Sciences, and Humanities\. Courses use a combination of big lectures and smaller classroom\-based seminar where dialogue \(often informal\) between lecturer and student is not only expected but central to teaching\. Most courses are followed by both Danish and international students giving students an opportunity to interact with local students on a day\-to\-day basis\. In addition, students can bond through social programing planned by AU everyday throughout Summer University\. The city of Aarhus was voted best student city in Denmark three years in a row and is one of the most liveable places on earth\!

More specific and finalized program details can be found on the partner institution's website\. However, you must apply through Go Global to be considered for this program and ensure you follow the appropriate transfer credit process\.  
 

## Who can go?

**This is experience is available via** [**summer exchange**](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/summer-abroad#summerabroadfaq) **for students from all faculties\.** 

-   All applicants must meet Go Global eligibility requirements

-   Arts
-   Commerce \(UBCV\)
-   Health Sciences
-   Management \(UBCO\)
-   Science

### Course load information

### Transfer credit

Check out the courses that previous students have transferred back to UBC in the last 5 years using our [Course Search Tool](https://tcp.goglobal.ubc.ca/search)\. If you don't see a particular course you listed, it simply means you need to submit it as a new course request through the [Transfer Credit Portal](https://tcp.goglobal.ubc.ca/) while on your Go Global experience\. For more information, please visit the [Go Global Transfer Credit webpage](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/transfer-credits-go-global "Transfer credits for Go Global")\.

**Not all courses listed are offered through the summer program at this partner institution\.** The tool is for reference only–research the partner's website for actual course offerings\.

[Search for previously approved courses](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/transfer-credits-go-global "Transfer credits for Go Global")

Note: Transfer credits are only granted for courses with academic content that meet the academic standard for UBC\. Courses that do not contain academic coursework may not be eligible\. Please visit [Go Global Transfer Credit webpage](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/transfer-credits-go-global "Transfer credits for Go Global") to learn more\. Please speak to a departmental advisor if you have any questions\.

### Other opportunities at this partner

title: ISCI 361/461: Bermuda Field Course – Systems Approaches to Regional Sustainability (Reading Week)
content_markdown:
#### Program Overview

**Location:** Bermuda, United Kingdom Overseas Territory  
**Course codes:** ISCI 361 / ISCI 461 \(3 credits\)  
**Faculty leads:** Dr\. [Denise Gabriel](mailto:gabriel@science.ubc.ca) and Dr\. Steven Quane \(Integrated Sciences\), Dr\. [Lee Groat](mailto:groat@mail.ubc.ca) \(Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences\)  
**Dates:** 

-   In country: February 13 \- 20, 2027 \(Reading Week\)
-   Overall program commitment: January 5 \- April 27, 2027

**Application deadline:** Tuesday, September 29, 2026 \(11:59pm PDT\)   
**Funding:** Eligible participants will receive a $1000 Go Global Award\.

##### **Applications open in mid\-September\.** 

[Click Here for Application Instructions](http://global.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/global-seminars/preparing-apply)

##### **Sign up for the Bermuda Field Course info session to learn more:** 

[Click Here to Sign Up for the Info Session](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_agDoGAjmnlL3w4S) 

### About the Course

Contemporary scientists agree that addressing complex global challenges such as environmental sustainability requires a systems thinking approach\. This means understanding how different elements interact within a whole, rather than examining them in isolation\. This 8\-day, 3 credit intensive course offers students the opportunity to explore these concepts through direct experience in Bermuda\. Students will engage with the island’s ecosystems, landscapes, and communities, while learning from local experts and residents about the historical and contemporary forces shaping Bermuda’s environment\. 

Bermuda is an ideal setting for systems\-based learning\. Its rich marine biodiversity, extensive coral reef systems, and visible impacts of climate change \- such as rising sea levels and ocean acidification \- offer a living laboratory for observation and analysis\. The island also provides insight into pressing issues like invasive species, marine conservation, and sustainable tourism\.  

Through immersive learning, students will develop a strong understanding of how environmental systems function and how human actions influence their stability\. This course equips students with the tools to think critically and holistically about sustainability challenges, both locally and globally\. 

Learn more about 5th Year ISCI student Nicole Tam's experience on the Iceland and Hawaii Field Courses: [***Global Insider: Exploring Sustainability from Iceland to Hawaii***](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/news/november-11-2025/global-insider-exploring-sustainability-iceland-hawaii)

### Program Eligibility

##### **General Global Seminar requirements**

To participate in a Global Seminar, students must:

-   Be in good\-standing in their faculty \(as defined by home faculty\)
-   In the year leading up to the Global Seminar, have full\-time student status \(as defined by home faculty\)
-   Have completed 2nd year requirements before the start of the program \(i\.e\. 3rd or 4th year standing\)
-   Have at least a 70% academic average in your last full\-time academic session before applying
-   Maintain a 70% academic average leading up to the program
-   Meet any program specific requirements listed below including pre\-requisites before participating

##### **Program\-specific requirements**

-   Students must have reached third\-year standing before the start of the program \(i\.e\. 3rd or 4th year\)\.
-   The course is primarily intended for Faculty of Science students, but undergraduates from other majors such as Environmental Science, Land and Food Systems, Arts, Commerce, and Engineering are also welcome to apply\.
-   ISCI 461 is only available to students who have already completed ISCI 361\.
-   Preference may be given to Integrated Sciences students if applications are competitive\.

**Final selection will be made by the lead faculty program directors\. Space in the program may be limited\.** 

Students who wish to participate in the summer after graduating may be eligible on a case\-by\-case basis\.

### Experience and Conditions in the Field

##### Daily schedule

---

This is an immersive, outdoor field course\. Students will be active most days from morning until evening, with evening group discussions to review the day’s activities and prepare for the next\.

##### Activities

---

Fieldwork may involve walking on uneven terrain and occasional boat travel\. Students will visit natural and cultural sites, meet with local experts, and take part in hands\-on learning activities, including at least one required snorkeling activity\.

##### Climate

---

Bermuda in February has mild, breezy weather with occasional rain\. Students should be prepared to spend extended time outdoors in variable conditions\.

##### Transportation

---

Local travel will include walking, public transit, ferries, and taxis or chartered vans as needed\.

##### Housing

---

Students will live together in a shared house, with approximately four students per room\. Accommodations include shared kitchen, bathrooms, and common areas\. Students are expected to contribute to a respectful and cooperative group environment\.

### Accessibility and Considerations

**We encourage students with accessibility concerns to reach out early to the lead faculty program directors to discuss potential accommodations and determine whether the program is a good fit for their needs\.**

##### Mobility and infrastructure

---

Bermuda has limited sidewalks and some field sites involve uneven terrain\. Transportation and accommodations may not be fully accessible for students who use wheelchairs or have limited mobility\.

##### Swimming requirement

---

At least one course activity involves snorkeling\. Students must be comfortable in the water and able to swim in order to participate safely\.

##### Physical activity

---

The course includes moderate activity such as walking, boat travel, and extended time outdoors\. Students should be prepared for active days in variable weather\.

##### Shared living

---

Students will stay in shared accommodations and are expected to contribute to a respectful and cooperative group environment\. Single rooms are not available\.

##### Dietary and personal needs

---

Most meals are self\-prepared in the shared kitchen\. Students with specific dietary requirements should be prepared to manage their needs in this context\.

### Program Fee and Costs

###### **Approximate program fee: $3900\-4200\***

*The final fee depends on the number of students enrolled\. All Global Seminars only run if a minimum number of students participate\.*

###### **Included:**

-   Accommodation in a shared house
-   Program\-related travel within Bermuda \(walking, ferries, taxis, or chartered vans as arranged\)
-   Excursions and entrance fees
-   Some group meals
-   On\-site guest lectures and activities

###### **Not Included:**

-   Go Global Fee \($440\.00\)
-   Flights
-   UBC tuition for credits
-   Visa/country entrance fees
-   Travel medical insurance
-   Most meals
-   Personal spending money/incidentals\*

\* Some examples of personal costs include: mobile communication, personal transportation that is not related to the learning outcomes of the program, additional meals that are not already identified as part of the Program Fee, immunizations, visas, etc\.

### Funding

**Go Global Award**

---

All eligible students in this Global Seminar will automatically receive a **$1,000 Go Global Award**\. No separate application is required\.

##### **Global Pathfinder Award**

---

The Global Pathfinder Award supports students who face barriers to participating in study abroad\. It provides **$2,000** for Summer Abroad, Global Seminar, or Research Abroad programs\. Students who have not previously participated in Go Global and who meet the eligibility criteria are encouraged to apply\.  
Students successful in their Pathfinder application will receive this award instead of the $1000 Go Global Award\. The awards do not stack\. 

[Learn more about the Global Pathfinder Award](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/awards-students-participating-go-global#:~:text=The%20Global%20Pathfinder%20Award%20%2D%20Closed)

### Program Safety

All travel and program activities involve risk of harm to participants\. Go Global and Seminar program leads take reasonable precautions to reduce risks\. However, not all harms can be anticipated or prevented\. 

While travelling on UBC programs, students have a responsibility for their own safety and the safety of the group\.

Some common issues for travellers include:

-   Illness and injuries \(e\.g\. respiratory illnesses, flu, food poisoning, sprained ankles, etc\.\)
-   Fatigue and heat exhaustion
-   Violence like robbery, or gender\- and race\-based harassment or attacks, especially in urban areas
-   Traffic accidents
-   Lost documents \(passports, credit cards, etc\.\)

**Before applying:**

-   Get to know the places you will be travelling by using available resources like [Global Affairs Canada travel reports](https://travel.gc.ca/travelling/advisories)\.
-   Consider your own mental and physical health alongside what you know about the conditions during the program \(e\.g\. how physical is the program? What are the living conditions? What can I do to prepare myself?\)

**Before departure:**  

-   Participate in all pre\-departure activities offered by Go Global and your program teaching team to learn about the program and ways to prevent and respond to incidents\.
-   Ensure you have adequate travel medical insurance that will cover you in the location and for the duration of your trip\.
-   Be aware of how to use your travel medical insurance, if you need it, and where to access medical care or other emergency assistance in the locations where you will be travelling\. 

**During the program:** 

-   If you don’t feel safe, say something\! Let your program leads know how you feel, or about incidents that occur\. Don’t hesitate to contact Go Global during your program\.
-   Know your own needs: be aware of your own mental and physical health and your limits\. Communicate with your program lead and group about making adjustments, as needed\. 

#### **Public health: COVID\-19 and other diseases**

Students and faculty are required to comply with the entry requirements of the host country, regulations of transportation carriers, and any local public health orders\. These rules might require vaccinations \(e\.g\. for COVID\-19, yellow fever, etc\.\) to enter the country or to participate in certain program activities\. Some places may require masking, testing or isolation in various circumstances\. It is your responsibility to research and comply with any requirements\.

COVID\-19 and other infections can spread easily in a group setting\. Most programs involve shared accommodations\. Unless required by local public health authorities, isolation for those infected during the program may not be possible\.   
   
Review local requirements before applying and before departure\. Check the [Global Affairs Canada Advisory](https://travel.gc.ca/travelling/advisories) under Entry Requirements for your Global Seminar destination to learn more\. Keep in mind that program conditions can vary and rules can change before or during your trip\.

-   Most courses  are available to exchange students, subject to vacancy
-   Exchange students should note that certain elective courses have pre\-requisites
-   A list of courses open to exchange students will be sent via email 6\-8 weeks prior to start of online course registration \- students may only select courses from the course list \(please DO NOT choose from the courses listed on the SMU website or any other sources\)
-   To view course descriptions, see [Course Catalogue / Class Search](http://eservices.smu.edu.sg/psp/ps/EMPLOYEE/HRMS/c/SIS_CR.SIS_CLASS_SEARCH.GBL) \(select the term you are searching for and "Courses with sections offered"\)

## Academic planning

### Term dates

-   UBC Term 2 \(UL Spring Semester\): Mid February \- Late June
    

Social Sciences, Business, Law, Geoscience and Biology:

-   UBC Term 2 \(UL Spring Semester\): Mid February \- Early July

-   Arts
-   Commerce \(UBCV\)
-   Education
-   Land and Food Systems
-   Management \(UBCO\)

    -   some courses in English in Biology, Economics and English Literature
-   Courses at the Master's level are taught in English and French
    -   UBC students in their 4th year can normally take Masters level courses on exchange at UNIL
-   UBC students normally take English literature and French as a second language courses at UNIL, or masters level courses in other areas\.
-   There is a good selection of courses in English in the [School of Business and Economics](https://www.unil.ch/hec/exchange/choice-of-courses) at UNIL\.

**Terms available:** Term 1, Term 2, Full year Term 1 \+ 2 \(UBC Term 1 start\)

[Apply](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/node/3146)

## Who can go?

-   Only Commerce students \(Vancouver\) may study at the KU Leuven [Faculty of Economics and Business](https://www.kuleuven.be/english/admissions/exchange)
-   Arts, LFS and Forestry students may study in the [Faculty of Arts](https://www.arts.kuleuven.be/english/education/leuven) and [Faculty of Bioscience](https://onderwijsaanbod.kuleuven.be/2024/opleidingen/e/SC_51315093.htm#activetab=voorwaarden)

## Academic planning

### Term dates

-   UBC Term 1 \(KU Leuven Semester 1\): mid\-September to late January \(exams in January can sometimes be written by distance\)
-   UBC Term 2 \(KU Leuven Semester 2\): Early February to early July  
     
-   Students on exchange in term 1 may be able to write some exams in December
    
-   Exams not available in December may sometimes be written in January at UBC
    
-   Coordination of invigilation and any related costs are the responsibility of the student \(please contact Go Global at least 4 weeks before the exam\)
    

### Areas of study available:

-   Arts
-   Commerce \(UBCV\)
-   Forestry
-   Land and Food Systems

### Course availability and restrictions

-   ARTS students may participate in [PECS Program](http://www.arts.kuleuven.be/pecs/), and may also enroll in non\-PECS courses, and choose from any of the 3 campuses
-   LFS and Forestry students may study in the [Faculty of Bioscience Engineering](https://www.biw.kuleuven.be/en) and Arts
    -   The Faculty of Bioscience Engineering has 7 MSc programmes taught in English\. Exchange students are able to pursue these programs given that they have sufficient academic background\.
    -   See the list of [Courses for Exchange Students in the Faculty of Bioscience Engineering \(Leuven\) \- Programme structure \| KU Leuven](https://onderwijsaanbod.kuleuven.be/opleidingen/e/SC_51315093.htm)
    -   Exchange students pursuing studies in the Faculty of Bioscience Engineering are required to take 50% of their coursework in the Faculty of Bioscience Engineering\. The other 50% of coursework may be taken in other faculties of KU Leuven\.
-   Study in the [Faculty of Economics & Business \(FEB\)](https://feb.kuleuven.be/eng/international/comingtofebonexchange/comingtofebonexchange) is open to COMM students only
-   COMM students may also choose from the main campus \(Leuven\), Antwerp or Brussels:[https://feb\.kuleuven\.be/eng/international/information\-package/courses](https://feb.kuleuven.be/eng/international/information-package/courses)
    -   **Leuven**: Courses in economics and finance tend to be very analytical \(bachelor students should be well versed in mathematics/statistics\)
    -   **Antwerp and Brussels**: Courses have a more hands\-on approach, with slightly less focus on quantitative skills and slightly more on management skills
        -   Antwerp: Undergraduate and Graduate \(Master of Science in Business Administration\) programs available for incoming exchange students
        -   Brussels: English\-taught Bachelor and Master of Science in Business Administration, an English\-taught Master of Science in Business Engineering as well as a MSc in International Business Economics and Management

[Partner Course Information](http://www.kuleuven.be/english/admissions/exchange/courses)

### Course equivalency Formula

-   ECTS credits divided by 2 \= UBC credits

### Course load Information

-   Minimum: 27 ECTS per semester
-   Maximum: 33 ECTS per semester

### Transfer credit

The [transfer credit process](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/transfer-credits-go-global "Transfer credits for Go Global") takes approximately 16 weeks following each submission deadline\. You should allow sufficient time to meet important deadlines that may affect you \(e\.g\. application for graduation, registration in courses that require prerequisites that you took on exchange, entry to a major/honours program, etc\.\)

[Search for previously approved courses](https://tcp.goglobal.ubc.ca/search)

### Additional note for language of instruction

-   Courses taught in Dutch and English in both undergraduate and graduate programs
-   [Leuven Language Institute](http://ilt.kuleuven.be/english/) offers Dutch language courses

### Other opportunities at this partner

**\*NEW\* Erasmus\+ Scholarship \(KA171\)**

-   The [Erasmus\+ Programme](https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/opportunities) provides funding for student, faculty and staff mobility between institutions in the European Union and their international partners\.
-   Two scholarships are provided by the Erasmus\+ Programme of the European Union
    -   One will be awarded to a student nominated to a one\-term exchange at KU Leuven during the 2027/8 academic year within the Faculty of Arts 
    -   One will be awarded to a student nominated to a one\-term exchange at KU Leuven during the 2027/8 academic year within the Faculty of Economics and Business
-   Scholarship Details:
    -   Monthly grant: 900 Euro/month
    -   One\-off travel grant: 1188 Euro
-   Additional funding is possible based on the factors outlined [here](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/2024-09/E%2B%20Top%20Up_Wageningen%20University_1.pdf): 250 Euro/month
-   Students who are matched to KU Leuven will be contacted by Go Global with further details on how to be considered for this award

content_markdown:
[Summer Abroad](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/career/international-experiences/summer-abroad/universidade-de-santiago-de-compostela-summer#)
