title: How to apply
content_markdown:
#### Important

If you are an eligible student, get started and submit your VIRS application as early as possible: **at least 15 weeks before the planned start date of your research\.** It will take us 1\-2 months for us to review VIRS applications and for you to receive your acceptance letter\. After receiving your letter, you will then need to apply for relevant immigration documents: Canadian visa and/or study permit\. 

Instructions on this page are intended for students doing research at UBC Vancouver Campus\. If you are researching at UBC Okanagan campus, please see instructions [here](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/global-engagement-office/go-global/visiting-international-research-student-at-ubc-okanagan/)

##### Before applying

1.  Make sure VIRS is the [appropriate program](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/node/2626) for you\.
2.  Ensure you meet the [eligibility requirements](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/visiting-international-research-students/eligibility-requirements "Eligibility requirements")\.
3.  Check that your research start date is realistic, especially if you need to obtain immigration documents for travel\. **\*Students who are planning a research study period of 6 months or more are advised to check the notice on the availability of Provincial Attestation Letter \(PALs\) \-\- a document required to apply for a study permit \-\- on** [**this page**](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/visiting-international-research-students/applying-your-initial-study-permit) **before submitting a VIRS application\.** 

***How do I know if my start date is realistic?*** 

*Check* [*processing times*](https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html) *for immigration documents based on your country of citizenship, then factor processing times into your start date\. \* For example, if you are applying in July for a October start and the listed processing time is 15 weeks, your research start date is not realistic\.* 

***\*Please note that there is currently a delay in processing times across the world and it is very likely you need to give yourself even more time than what is posted\.*** 

4.  Download and complete the required application documents\. Collect all required signatures\.
    -   Attach a VIRS Approval Form to your application\. \(Scanned copies are OK\.\) Save the Approval Form in PDF or JPEG format\.
        -   VIRS students can only be admitted for up to one year maximum in the initial application\. For extension beyond a year, see guidelines in "Withdrawals and Extensions" on [this page](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/visiting-international-research-students/info-current-accepted-students)\.
    -   Are you interested in the [Joint Doctoral Research Student \(JDRS\) designation](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/visiting-international-research-students/prospective-students "Prospective students") and eligible? Complete the [Joint Doctoral Research Scholar \(JDRS\) Request Form \(PDF\)](https://global.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/documents/JDRS_form_Dec-6-22.pdf) to apply\. Save the Approval Form in PDF or JPEG format\.

##### Ready to apply? 

Since it could take up to two months for application review, submit as soon as possible\! The VIRS application processing time will depend on the overall number of applications Go Global receives\. **We are not able to rush or expedite letters of acceptance based on your individual situation\.** Thank you for your patience in this process\.

###### How to apply

1.  Create an account through the [VIRS Student Application Portal](https://goglobal.students.ubc.ca/ggapplications/s/create-account)\. **Use an email address you check regularly and plan to use throughout the application process\.** We will send email you important updates about your VIRS application through this email address\. Make sure @ubc\.ca emails are on your safe list\.
2.  After you create an account, check your email for instructions on how to begin the application\. 
3.  Fill out the application and upload the necessary documents\. Please use the same email address in application that you used to create your account\.
    1.  the [VIRS Approval Form](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/2026-09/VIRS%20Approval%20Form%20Sept%202026.pdf)
    2.  the [JDRS Request Form](http://global.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/documents/JDRS_form_Dec-6-22.pdf) \(if applicable\)\.
    3.  Identity Document
    4.  Proof of enrolment from your home institution
        1.  Please upload a letter **written in English** showing your enrollment as a student at your home unversity\. **The letter is only sufficient if it can prove that you will maintain enrolment at your home university for the entire duration of the research period indicated on your VIRS application\.** 
        2.  Please ensure that the letter is issued on official letterhead and dated within the last six months
        3.  Note: Copies of academic transcripts or a student card are not acceptable
4.  Submit your application\. 

###### After you’ve submitted   

1.  Check your email again for your new UBC student number\.
2.  Pay your VIRS program fee \($440\.00\)\* [online](https://secure.touchnet.net/C20435_ustores/web/store_main.jsp?STOREID=35&SINGLESTORE=true)\.    
    a\. Select “VIRS Program Fee” \(CAD440\.00\)\* > select “Add to cart” > provide your name, email \(the same one you used to submit your VIRS application\) and your UBC student number > select “Check out” > enter your email address again > provide your payment details\.
3.  We aim to have your UBC acceptance letter ready within 1\-2 months of receiving your VIRS program fee, depending on the volume of applications\.

\*Note: The VIRS Program Fee is subject to change year to year\. 

##### Next: I have my letter of acceptance\. Now what?

1.  **Verify your personal information** \(for example, legal name, date of birth, permanent address, etc\.\) is correct on your student application in the Go Global Student Application Portal and on the VIRS Letter of Acceptance\. If the information needs to be updated, you MUST notify Go Global within five business days of the email notification about your admission and prior to accepting your offer of admission\.
2.  **Accept your UBC admission offer in the Applicant Service Centre\.** Your acceptance to UBC is only confirmed after you accept your admission offer\. You have three weeks from the date of your acceptance letter to accept your offer\. **Ensure you are accepting offer to the correct UBC campus\.**
3.  **Create your Campus Wide Login \(CWL\)** account using your UBC student number\.
4.  **Apply for the appropriate immigration document using your letter of acceptance\. Do not delay this step** if you need immigration documents\. Documents can include a study permit and/or Temporary Resident Visa, or Electronic Travel Authorization, if applicable\.
    1.  Students engaged in research for **six \(6\) months or less** can complete their research under visitor status with a Temporary Resident Visa or Electronic Travel Authorization, depending on citizenship\.
    2.  Students engaged in research for **longer than six \(6\) months** require a study permit\.   
        Please note there have been changes made to the study permit application process\. To see the most recent updates and to determine what immigration document to obtain, please see [this page](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/visiting-international-research-students/applying-your-initial-study-permit)\. Check estimated [processing times](http://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/services/application/check-processing-times.html) for various immigration document applications on the Government of Canada website\.
5.  **Pay your iMED fees** through [Workday](https://workday.students.ubc.ca/logging-into-workday/)\. Log into your account using your CWL \(see step 3 above\)\.  

Students admitted through VIRS will be registered as full\-time students at UBC for the duration of their research period\. Admitted students will have permission to engage in research education, but cannot register for academic courses\.  

##### Application troubleshooting

### I am having trouble creating an account\.

Please try the following and if you are still experiencing difficulties, please contact [go\.global@ubc\.ca](mailto:go.global@ubc.ca):

1.  Clear the cache and browsing history on your web browser;
2.  Try creating your account using the incognito mode on your web browser;
3.  Try creating your account on another web browser\.

### I have created an account, but I can't log back\-in\. 

1.  Try logging in directly to the [VIRS application](http://goglobal.students.ubc.ca/ggapplications) using your existing email address \(the same email address you used to create your account\) for your username\.
2.  If you are unable to log in, click “Forgot your password?” to create a new password\.
3.  If you are still experiencing difficulties, contact us\.

If you need to change the start or end dates of your research, complete this [Delayed Arrival Online Form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_ba5VaYUUclYNwSq) to ensure your acceptance letter is accurate and that you have appropriate insurance coverage\. 

If you are not sure when your new research start and end dates will be, please select: "I am not sure when my new arrival date will be" in the form above\. 

##### Fees and additional information

-   Land and Food Systems

### Course availability and restrictions

-   Maximum: 60 Bangor credits per semester or 120 Bangor credits per year
    -   students who stay for one year can take 70 credits in Semester 1 and 50 credits in Semester 2, if required
    -   Half\-module \= 5 Bangor credits
    -   Single module \= 10 Bangor credits
    -   Double\-module \= 20 Bangor credits
    -   A single 10 credit module involves around 100 hours of student time divided between direct contact, directed study, private study and assessment
-   Undergraduate modules range from Level 1\-3
-   Level 4 modules are Post\-graduate

title: Do I need a Meal Plan?
content_markdown:
##### Do I need a Meal Plan?

Residence Meal Plans are only required if you are living in Orchard Commons, Totem Park or Place Vanier\. If you have been placed in a residence other than the three mentioned above, you are not required to purchase a meal plan as you will have a kitchen in your unit\.

For more information about meal plans at UBC, please see [this website](https://food.ubc.ca/meal-plans/residence-meal-plan-all-access-dining/)\. Contact [Student Housing and Hospitality Services](http://vancouver.housing.ubc.ca/contact-us) for any questions\.

**Program dates:** Sessions run from June through July

[Apply](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/node/3658)

## About the program

HEC Paris \(Ecole des Hautes Etudes Commerciales de Paris\) offers two summer sessions, each consisting of 2\-week intensive programs centred on business topics\. Students can participate in one program per session, up to two programs total during the full summer period\. Highlights include seminars with leading professors and industry professionals, hands\-on learning, case studies, groupwork, and networking events on campus\.

More specific and finalized program details can be found on the partner institution's website\. However, you must apply through Go Global to be considered for this program and ensure you follow the appropriate transfer credit process\.

## Who can go?

**This is experience is available via** [**summer exchange**](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/summer-abroad#summerabroadfaq) **and is limited to** **Commerce students at UBCV only**

-   All applicants must meet Go Global eligibility requirements
    -   [**UBC Vancouver students**](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/summer-abroad/eligibility "Eligibility")
    -   [**UBC Okanagan students**](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/global-engagement-office/go-global/outbound-short-term-programs/summer-abroad/)

## Academic planning

### Areas of study available:

-   Commerce \(UBCV\)

### Course equivalency formula

-   2 ECTS credits \= 1 UBC credit

### Course load information

-   Take one program maximum per session\. Each session is worth 5 ECTS credits

### Transfer credit

Check out the courses that previous students have transferred back to UBC in the last 5 years using our [Course Search Tool](https://tcp.goglobal.ubc.ca/search)\. If you don't see a particular course you listed, it simply means you need to submit it as a new course request through the [Transfer Credit Portal](https://tcp.goglobal.ubc.ca/) while on your Go Global experience\. For more information, please visit the [Go Global Transfer Credit webpage](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/transfer-credits-go-global "Transfer credits for Go Global")\.

**Not all courses listed are offered through the summer program at this partner institution\.** The tool is for reference only–research the partner's website for actual course offerings\.

[Search for previously approved courses](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/transfer-credits-go-global "Transfer credits for Go Global")

Note: Transfer credits are only granted for courses with academic content that meet the academic standard for UBC\. Courses that do not contain academic coursework may not be eligible\. Please visit [Go Global Transfer Credit webpage](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/transfer-credits-go-global "Transfer credits for Go Global") to learn more\. Please speak to a departmental advisor if you have any questions\.

content_markdown:

[Map from: Google Maps](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/styles/square_600/public/2024-08/University%20College%20London_0.jpg?itok=xRs99YHd)

**Location:** London, United Kingdom  
**Language of instruction:** English  
**Tuition payable to:** UBC  
**Program website:** [University College London Exchange Website](http://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/international/study-abroad/affiliate)  
**Terms available:** Term 1, Term 2, Full year Term 1 \+ 2 \(UBC Term 1 start\)

[Apply](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/node/3146)

## Who can go?

-   This partner has a minimum cumulative average requirement of 77%
-   2 years of prior university study completed upon entry to UCL
-   Students from all Faculties may attend UCL, but not all Faculties at UCL are available to exchange students\. Please pay careful attention to the Faculties that are available at UCL under Course Information and Restrictions\. Students should review the Study Abroad guide for the [list of academic departments](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/study-abroad-at-ucl/subjects), any subject\-specific entry requirements and any restrictions\. For example, some departments do not accept students for Term 1 only, and some accept students for the full academic year only\.
-   Please note that the English department is not open to exchange students\. For more restrictions, [please review this page](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/study-abroad-at-ucl/study-options/your-study-options)\.
-   Students wishing to take Modules in Management must attend Full Year or Term 2 only
-   Students wishing to study the [Natural Sciences](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/study-abroad-at-ucl/subjects/natural-sciences) offerings must attend the Full Year\. There are two pathways offered: **Neuroscience, Psychology and Physics**, and **Genetics, Evolution and Ethics**\. Each pathway has a separate list of modules and subject entry requirements\. 

## Academic planning

### Term dates

-   UBC Term 1 \(UCL  Autumn semester\): Late September to Late December
-   UBC Term 2 \(UCL Spring and Summer semester\): Early January to Mid June
-   Full Year: \(Late September to Mid June\)

***\*Students arriving in January must stay for the Spring and Summer terms\.***

### Areas of study available:

-   Arts
-   Commerce \(UBCV\)
-   Engineering
-   Health Sciences
-   Land and Food Systems
-   Science

### Course availability and restrictions

-   Although a preliminary selection is made at the time of application, course enrolment does not take place until arrival at UCL, when students discuss their programme of study with their academic advisor \(called the Affiliate Student Tutor\)
-   Most students must take at least 50% of their modules within the parent department\. Students may be able to take up to 50% of their modules in other departments; however, this is not guaranteed, and students should be prepared to take 100% of their modules within their department\. Students may be considered for modules in other departments where the department is open to Affiliates during their period of study, and there is capacity on modules, and where students meet any eligibility criteria\.When selecting modules outside of their parent department, students should be aware that they will be not be prioritized\.
-   Please note that module approval is at departments’ discretion and students are not guaranteed access to any particular modules, even within their home department\. Students must be flexible when selecting modules\.
-   There is a small number of modules that cannot cater to Fall\-only students; however, now the majority of modules do, as arrangements can be made for alternative examination times
-   Students may take courses in the following Faculties at UCL:
    -   **Faculty of Engineering Sciences**
        -   Electronic and Electrical Engineering students can only apply for a Term 2 or Full\-Year
        -   Mechanical Engineering
        -   Biochemical Engineering, Students can only take courses as Full Year or Term 2
        -   Chemical Engineering, Students can only take courses as Full Year or Term 2
        -   Civil, Environmental & Geomatic Engineering
        -   Management courses are offered through the Faculty of Engineering Sciences\. Students can only take courses as Full Year or Term 2\.
        -   Very limited access to Computer Science \(CS\)
            -   Students wishing to study in CS must have a background in CS, have studied at least 3 CS modules per year, and cannot attend UCL in their final year of studies
            -   Students in CS can take at most **one non\-CS** **module** in each term
            -   Students in CS must go to UCL for the Full Year or Term 2 to gain registration in CS courses
            -   Students going to UCL for Term 1 only will be ***unable*** to register into any CS courses\.
    -   **Faculty of Mathematical & Physical Sciences**
        -   Chemistry
        -   Earth Sciences
        -   History and Philosophy of Science
        -   Mathematics, Students can only take courses as Full Year or Term 2
        -   Physics & Astronomy, Students can only take courses as Full Year or Term 2
        -   Statistical Sciences, Students can only take courses as Full Year or Term 2
        -   Students wishing to study the [Natural Sciences](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/study-abroad-at-ucl/subjects/natural-sciences) offerings must attend the Full Year\. There are two pathways offered: **Neuroscience, Psychology and Physics**, and **Genetics, Evolution and Ethics**\. Each pathway has a separate list of modules and subject entry requirements\.
    -   **Faculty of Social & Historical Sciences**
        -   Anthropology
        -   Archaeology
        -   Economics
        -   Geography
        -   History
        -   Political Science and International Relations
        -   The Americas
    -   **Faculty of Life Sciences**
        -   Biological Sciences
        -   Biomedical Sciences
        -   Molecular Biosciences
        -   Neuroscience
    -   **Faculty of Brain Sciences**
        -   Psychology
        -   Psychology and Language Sciences
        -   Linguistics
    -   **Faculty of Arts and Sciences**
        -   Within the Faculty of Arts and Humanities, the Department of Arts and Sciences \(BASc\) is available to exchange students; however, other programs such as English, Philosophy and Languages are not

[Search for courses at this institution](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/study-abroad-ucl/study-abroad-guide/subjects)

### Course equivalency Formula

-   UCL credits divided by 4 \= UBC credits

### Course load Information

-   Normal Courseload: 120 UCL Credits for full year or 60 UCL Credits for one semester

### Transfer credit

The [transfer credit process](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/transfer-credits-go-global "Transfer credits for Go Global") takes approximately 16 weeks following each submission deadline\. title: UBC & VinUni Student Research Forum 2023
content_markdown:
## How to advance human development in the global age, while protecting the planet and cultural identity? Learning from Vietnam

### **About the program**

**Dates:** May 20, 2023 \- May 31, 2023  
**Location:** VinUniversity Campus, Hanoi, Vietnam

This is a 10\-day, well\-funded, research forum for students\. This is an opportunity UBC and VinUniversity students to come together, problem\-solve on the world's toughest issues, and co\-create original research\. With mixed teams involving students from both universities, the forum consists of the following:

-   Expert Lectures & discussions
-   Group work and problem\-solving
-   Pre\-assignments to prepare for group work
-   Field trips and site visits around Hanoi
-   Final presentations at VinUni
-   Final individual report

**Theme:** How to advance human development in the global age, while protecting the planet and cultural identity?

-   ***National identity and social equity:*** How can a country balance openness to the global economy with preserving national identity, dealing with social equality, protecting national culture, protecting the environment?  
-   ***Digital engagement and misinformation:*** How should we benefit from digital opportunities for development while dealing with digital problems, such as misinformation, online violence, cultural insensitivity?
-   ***Climate change:*** How can we accelerate climate change prevention and response? What can we learn from Vietnam’s actions in this regard?
-   ***Biodiversity:*** Protecting biodiversity in the spirit of the new UN Biodiversity Framework: what can we learn from Vietnam’s experience and initiatives? 
-   ***Public health and pandemics:*** Dealing with pandemics: what can we learn from Vietnam’s experience with Covid?
-   ***Trade and economic inequality:***  How to balance the integration into trade agreements \(CPTPP, RCEP, etc\) and integrated in global supply chains, while take care of disadvantaged groups falling behind, manage social crises and support indigenous people\.
-   ***Geopolitical tensions and instability:*** At a time of growing disruptions and tensions about great powers, what course should middle powers and mid\-size countries take? How can they support each other to bring stability and mutual benefits?

While working with their groups, students will attend lectures offered by faculty members from UBC and Vin\-Uni on the topic, and take part in field trips and site\-visits around the Hanoi area\.

UBC students will have the opportunity to learn about Vietnamese culture and politics first\-hand while receiving mentorship from distinguished professors from both UBC and Vin\-Uni\. 

**About VinUniversity:** 

[https://vinuni\.edu\.vn/](https://vinuni.edu.vn/)

[Embedded content: YouTube video player](https://www.youtube.com/embed/RFikpr2jHJo)

*"VinUniversity is a private, not\-for\-profit university established by Vingroup – the largest private conglomerate in Vietnam\. VinUni aspires to become a university of excellence with a mission to develop talents for the future\.VinUniversity comprises of College of Arts and Sciences; College of Business and Management; College of Engineering and Computer Science; and College of Health Sciences\. Every aspect of the University: its curricula, research, faculty, student body, facilities, and campus life, is developed to meet the highest standards set by the world’s leading accrediting and ranking organizations, such as ABET, AACSB, Quacquarelli Symonds \(QS\), and Times Higher Education \(THE\)\."*

**UBC Academic Sponsor: Dr\. Yves Tiberghien:**

[https://politics\.ubc\.ca/profile/yves\-tiberghien/](https://politics.ubc.ca/profile/yves-tiberghien/)

Yves Tiberghien is a Professor of Political Science and Konwakai Chair in Japanese Research at the University of British Columbia \(UBC\) in Vancouver, Canada\. He is also Director Emeritus of the Institute of Asian Research, and Director of the Center for Japanese Research\. He is a regular visiting professor at Tokyo University \(Graduate School of Public Policy\) and at Sciences Po Paris \(Paris School of International Affairs\)\. He has held other visiting positions at National Chengchi University \(Taiwan\), GRIPS \(Tokyo\), and the Jakarta School of Public Policy \(Indonesia\)\. Yves’ research specializes in comparative political economy and global economic and environmental governance, with an empirical focus on Japan, China, Korea, and Europe\.

**VinUniversity Faculty and lecture topics:** 

-   Prof\. David Harrison: Cultural diversity and Biodiversity in Vietnam\.
    -   [https://vinuni\.edu\.vn/people/k\-david\-harrison\-phd/](https://vinuni.edu.vn/people/k-david-harrison-phd/%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0)   
-   Prof\. Jason Picard: Exploring architecture and power
    -   [https://vinuni\.edu\.vn/people/jason\-picard/](https://vinuni.edu.vn/people/k-david-harrison-phd/%C2%A0%C2%A0%C2%A0)
-    Dr\. Michael Clark:  Asian perspectives on topics in social epistemology, including such topics as learning from others, responding reasonably to disagreements, and expertise\. We will be especially concerned with these topics in connection to the informational environment shaped by social media platforms\.
    -   [https://vinuni\.edu\.vn/people/michael\-clark/](https://vinuni.edu.vn/people/michael-clark/)
-   Dr\. Anupama Devendrakumar: a lecture on Vietnam’s international trade in ASEAN context
    -   [https://vinuni\.edu\.vn/people/anupama\-devendrakumar\-phd/](https://vinuni.edu.vn/people/anupama-devendrakumar-phd/)

---

### **Student eligibility**

About 12 \- 15 UBC students will be selected to participate: Undergraduate students or graduate students are eligible to apply, though priority will be given to senior undergraduate students\. Successful applicants should demonstrate a strong academic performance, interest and experiences in extra\-curricular activities, and be a good team\-player\.

-   Full time undergraduate or graduate students \(minimum 18 credits in the 2022\-23 academic year\)
-   Minimum 70% academic average overall, and in Term 1 2022
-   Currently 2nd year status or higher \(including students finishing their degree requirements this term and graduating in May\)
-   Students from any faculty are eligible
-   Students from both UBC\-V and UBC\-O are eligible
-   Highly motivated students who possess a strong interest in the forum themes\. Prior to the forum, participants should prepare themselves for fruitful discussion by researching on a specific topic of their interest relevant to the main theme\.
    

### Fees and Funding

Participation Fee: **$415\.00 \(Go Global Fee\) charged to selected students who accept their spot in the program\.** 

The UBC\-VinUni Student Forum will bear the costs for:

-   Accommodation expenses in Hanoi
-   A few meals will be provided throughout the conference, but students should expect to bear the majority of food costs
-   Field trip fees

Students are responsible for the costs of:

-   Flights
-   Meals
-   Incidental expenses at accommodation
-   Passport and Visa acquisition fees
-   Travel insurance

Participating students will receive a **Go Global Award of $1000** that can be used towards the costs of participating\. 

### How to apply

**Application deadline:** March 21, 2023 at 4 pm\.

There is no application fee\. 

Complete the application online through Go Global's [Gateway system](http://ubc-horizons.symplicity.com/student)\. Go to "Search Experiences" and search "forum" scroll to this program and press "Apply for" and select "Summer" to start an application\.

In your application you will be asked to respond to questions relating to: 

-   Your motivation for joining this program
-   How this program will benefit you in your current academic program and support your career goals
-   Any experience working on a team
-   Your interest and/or experience in community engagement or service

You will be asked to rank your interest in the program topics listed above\.

Please also upload your most up\-to\-date resume/CV\. 

Selected students will be notified by April 4\.

title: Global Insider: Exploring Europe, Academics, and Exchange Life at Sciences Po Reims
content_markdown:
UBC student Deborah Ojo reflects on how her exchange at Sciences Po Reims opened the door to European travel, meaningful friendships, and a new global academic perspective\.

February 3, 2026

*Are you a UBC undergrad thinking about going on a student exchange? It can be a daunting decision\. You might wonder, what's it like spending a year or a semester in another country? How can you prepare? And how do you handle it when things go sideways? We talked with a group of* [*UBC Global Ambassadors*](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/new-student-experiences/global-ambassadors-and-global-cultural-ambassadors) *who studied abroad with a* [*Go Global program*](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global)*\. They spoke with us candidly, sharing their personal impressions, fears and misgivings, best memories, top tips and advice\. \(This story is part of a series of Global Exchange Insider interviews\.\)* 

*Meet Deborah Ojo, a fourth year Commerce student studying Accounting and International Business\. She is originally from the Toronto, ON, Canada\.*

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Deborah%20Ojo%20Photo%203.JPG)

*Deborah Ojo at the major shopping strip in Porto, Portugal called Rua de Santa Catarina\. \(Taken by, Anonymous\)*

#### Before you go   

**Why did you pick the** [**Sciences Po Reims**](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/exchange/sciences-po-reims-and-paris "Sciences Po Reims and Paris") **for your exchange? How did you hear about it?**    
Ever since high school, I had dreamed of seeing Europe\. I had never travelled beyond North America and my home country of Nigeria, so when the chance came to apply for an exchange, I knew exactly what I wanted: a school that would let me experience Europe to the fullest, both in and out of the classroom\. As an avid reader of French and British writers such as Austen and Camus, I also knew I wanted to apply to programs that would allow me to study literature through a European lens, an opportunity my Accounting degree rarely afforded me\. During this search, I came across two schools: [Bocconi University](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/exchange/universita-commerciale-luigi-bocconi "Università Commerciale Luigi Bocconi") and [Sciences Po](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/exchange/sciences-po-reims-and-paris "Sciences Po Reims and Paris")\. My first choice was actually Bocconi, but I ended up getting matched to Sciences Po Paris instead\. You can imagine my initial disappointment at not being matched to my first choice\. However, I reminded myself that Paris could be just as fun\. I mean it's Paris, right?

Funnily enough, after being matched to Paris, I came across the Sciences Po Reims campus and one night at 2:00AM, I spontaneously requested to be switched\. Why? I saw that they offered a class on Jane Austen\. Little did I know, that random late\-night choice would ended up changing my life\! 

As one would expect, soon after this late night spontaneous decision, I had my doubts\. I became quite worried that I wouldn't like Reims, and even tried to switch back to Paris\. When switching back wasn't a possibility, I felt afraid I wouldn't enjoy my exchange\. While I felt slight regret for not sticking with Paris, I tried to remind myself that everything happens for a reason\. To calm my nerves I did a lot of research about Reims and I soon discovered what an amazing location it truly was\. 

Firstly, living in Reims made life just a bit cheaper in terms of rent and groceries\. It was also the heart of the Champagne District, making it a small town with a rich and unique culture\. Additionally, the courses offered at Sciences Po Reims were very unique, ranging from classes on African film and British literature, to global politics\. The thing that made the Sciences Po Reims campus stand out the most was the campus itself\. The Sciences Po Reims campus was smaller than the Paris campus, making it easier to navigate, especially for someone like me who is quite bad with directions\. The smaller campus also ended up making it easier for me to meet people, since the student body was very small\. All of this made the Sciences Po Reims campus an unexpected yet perfect location to live out my high school dreams\.

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Image%2011.JPG)

*The Reims Notre Dame \(Taken by, Deborah Ojo\)*

**What was the application process like? Any tips?**   
The application process was fairly straightforward, and Go Global offered many supporting resources to assist during the process, so my tip is to not stress, as long as you ensure you are adhering to the deadlines and doing your due diligence\. The hardest part was actually choosing the school I wanted to go to and the courses I wanted to take for the study plan\. There are so many options through exchange and it can feel overwhelming if you don’t have a clear direction\. My tip is to consider feasibility: how will going to the school affect your degree planning? How will the cost of living in that country impact you? How difficult will it be to get the needed travel documents?

As a Sauder student I could either go to a school which offered commerce courses, or only take electives while abroad\. In order to fully experience Europe, fulfil my dream of studying literature, and to avoid any complications with transferring credits, I opted to only take electives at Sciences Po\. Secondly, the cost of living in Reims seemed to be similar to, if not less than Vancouver, which made the location more appealing\. Lastly, through speaking to previous students who’d gone to France for exchange, I learned that getting the needed travel documents was very feasible if I planned properly\. The hardest of the three to evaluate for me was definitely course selection\. Transferring credits back to UBC can get complicated, so my recommendation is to do the appropriate preparations and meet with Go Global before applying\.

**How did you prepare? Anything to be aware of? \(travel, cultural differences, classes, etc\.\)**   
The biggest part of preparation for me was finding housing and applying for a visa\. To find my housing I relied on the resources provided to me by Go Global and Sciences Po\. They offered a list of common residences and apartments that exchange students used, and I spent a lot of time vetting each location and applying for tenancy\. For Reims, be aware that student housing is very limited, so I would highly recommend finding accommodation through an external residency such as [MGEL Logement](https://mgellogement.fr/), [Sharies](https://sharies.co/en/city/reims) or [KLEY](https://www.kley.fr/en/student-residence/reims)\. You can also utilise the Sciences Po housing portal to find a student friendly landlord, as there are many nice apartments around campus that are closer to the Sciences Po Reims Campus\. As for the Visa application, the hardest part is getting an appointment\. Be aware that appointments are limited, so get ahead and start looking for slots as soon as you can\. When it comes time to attend your appointment, make sure to be prepared, and print absolutely everything\! I made the mistake of forgetting to print a photocopy of my passport and other identification documents, and ended up paying extra to have them do it for me\.

**What worries did you have beforehand? How did you overcome the anxiety?**  
My biggest worry was about making friends\. My French isn’t very strong and so I feared the language barrier would limit my ability to socialize\. I feared feeling homesick and missing out on things as a lot of my friends were still at UBC when I decided to go on exchange\. To overcome my anxiety I made sure to put myself out there, and to say yes to as many opportunities as possible, whether that was taking a spontaneous trip to Brussels, sending a random text in the exchange group chat inviting people to lunch, or simply saying yes to a night out with new friends\. Through getting out of my comfort zone, I met an amazing group of girls who I travelled with, and who made my exchange experience a million times better\. I also made sure to put in effort in keeping up with what was going on back home\. I felt less homesick through doing weekly calls with my friends\!

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Deborah%20Ojo%20Photo%201.JPG)

*Deborah \(middle\) and her friends Francesca \(left\) and Ana \(right\) in front of the Eiffel Tower in Paris, France \(Taken by, Anonymous\)*

#### During the experience

**How was the overall experience? What did you learn?**   
The overall experience was unforgettable\. Being able to experience more than 5 countries and more than 10 different cities was new, exciting and eye opening, especially for someone who hadn't travelled much before\. The ease and affordability of travelling across Europe from France, paired with my light courseload made it very easy for me to take weekend trips with friends to places like Brussels, Porto, London, and Barcelona, while still engaging myself in my coursework\.

Contrary to some assumptions, living in Reims did not hinder my ability to experience the rest of France, in particular, Paris\. In fact, I travelled to Paris quite often, sometimes to visit friends, other times just to get my hair done or enjoy the pastries and hot chocolate at the popular café, [Carette](https://paris-carette.fr/)\. There was a 30 minute train that went straight to the heart of Paris directly from Reims, and if that didn’t work, I took what quickly became my best friend on exchange, a Flixbus\.

Additionally, the exchange community at Sciences Po Reims was extremely friendly, outgoing and tight\-knit\. I was able to make friends with people from all across Europe and the globe\! Looking back, the best memories I made were through exploring Reims itself and experiencing what everyday life is like in a French town\. The morning coffee with friends, afternoon picnics in the park, midnight snacks at Le Mediterranée, and long walks under the Christmas lights down Rue Gambetta created lifelong memories that I’ll never forget\. I wouldn’t have been able to experience any of these things had I not said yes to new friendships and opportunities, and so I think the biggest thing I learned was not being afraid to say yes\!

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Deborah%20Ojo%20Photo%209%20%281%29.JPG)

*Breakfast at Carette in Paris, France \(Taken by, Deborah Ojo\)*

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Deborah%20Ojo%20Photo%206.JPG)

*The Grand\-Place Square in Brussels, Belgium \(Taken by, Deborah Ojo\)*

**If you could change something or do it differently, what would you change or do?**   
Looking back, I wish I did more solo trips\! I had so much fun travelling with my friends, but I also ended up doing a solo trip to Wales and London near the end of my exchange and had so much fun\! During this trip I got to visit family, do a boat load of shopping, try different restaurants and even catch up with old high school friends\. That experience made me realize that solo tripping is such a unique and fun experience, and depending on the city, it can be much easier to find hotels or get tickets to certain excursions when going solo\. I didn’t do as much solo tripping out of fear, but looking back as long as you plan, there isn’t much to worry about\. I’d say if you get the chance while on exchange, try and go on at least one trip by yourself\.

**How were the academics?**   
I found the academics at Sciences Po Reims to be lighter than that of UBC\. The classes were much smaller and heavily participation based, with the exams being mainly essay writing or a final presentation\. We didn’t get much homework, if any, and when we did receive homework it was usually light reading\. As someone who enjoys reading and writing, I found this to be very manageable\. The content of the classes were also very unique\. I was able to learn about the history of Global Sociological Debates, Feminist European literature, and African American history, all topics I hadn’t had the chance to dive deeper into due to my major in Accounting\. I found this different learning experience to be extremely engaging\. Two classes in particular stuck out to me: Documenting Africa, which allowed me to study films by filmmakers from my home country, Nigeria, and Power, Professions, and Politics, where I explored Victorian\-era feminist British literature and even studied my favourite author, Jane Austen\. Due to the smaller class sizes, I was also able to bond with my professors, and make close friends through my classes\. Additionally, my course schedule worked out so that I only had classes on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays\! This gave me a four\-day weekend, which I often spent exploring both the city and Europe as a whole\.

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Deborah%20Ojo%20Photo%204%20%281%29.JPG)

*Casa Batlló, one of the Gaudi Houses located on Passeig de Gràcia in Barcelona, Spain \(Taken by Deborah Ojo\)*

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Deborah%20Ojo%20Photo%208.JPG)

*Playa de la Barceloneta in Barcelona, Spain \(Taken by, Deborah Ojo\)*

**How was the social aspect?**  
Through exchange I was able to meet so many amazing friends\. I found that the strongest bonds were with fellow exchange students\. On one of my first days at Sciences Po I went to a party, and spontaneously met another exchange student who added me to a group chat with other exchange students\. The next day I invited members of the group chat to grab lunch, and through the lunch I met some of my closest friends from my exchange experience\!

A unique aspect of the Sciences Po Reims campus is that the non\-exchange students are all in either their first or second year of university\. The Reims campus offers a distinctive three\-year program where students spend their first two years at Sciences Po and their final year abroad\. This structure, paired with how small the campus is, created many orientation events that were designed for first years, but were also welcome to and well attended by exchange students\. All the fun orientation events filled my first few weeks at Science Po with exciting events such as parties, scavenger hunts, competitions and city tours\. Through these events it was incredibly easy to meet fellow exchange students and from close bonds\. We created weekly routines and went to hang\-out spots, like Tuesdays at Ma Boutielle, or Thursdays at Lescale, and spent our weekends planning which city we would travel to next\. This routine made being in such a new environment feel less daunting\.

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Untitled%20design%20%281%29.png)

*Deborah \(left\) and her friend Kate \(right\) on the Dom Luís I Bridge in Porto, Portugal \(Taken by Anonymous\)*

[Image](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/inline-images/Deborah%20Ojo%20Photo%207.JPG)

*Sciences Po Reims orientation event in front of the Notre Dame in Reims, France \(Taken by Deborah Ojo\)*

#### After the experience

**Would you recommend this experience to others? What can they look forward to?**   
I would definitely recommend exchange to others\! My exchange experience was an amazing opportunity to integrate myself in a new environment, engage in a new learning style and make new friends\. Seeing a different side of the world was life changing\!

**What was the impact on your academic and personal development?**    
I gained a lot of confidence and independence on exchange\. Going to a totally new country, let alone a continent, all by myself, was daunting, but oftentimes we learn the most when pushed out of our comfort zone\. Experiences such as lugging my three massive suitcases by myself from Paris to Reims, moving into a new home alone, and navigating transit systems in a different language alone, strengthened my independence and thus confidence in myself\. I now feel more comfortable in new environments and more confident in my ability to take on new things\. I also feel more eager to travel the world\! Experiencing even a little of how diverse and vibrant the world is has sparked a dream in me to one day travel to at least two countries in every continent\. I also learned so much about global politics, cultures and issues while on exchange through befriending such a diverse group of people\. This, compounded with the impact of being in an academically rigorous environment which focused on shaping a strong international lens in students, has made me look at what I learn at UBC from a more global lens\.

**Read more Go Global** [**student stories**](https://global.ubc.ca/go-global/student-experiences/student-stories)**\.** 

---

title: McGill University
content_markdown:
[Exchange](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/exchange/mcgill-university#)

[https://www\.mcgill\.ca/newsroom/media\-gallery/detail/149441/73063](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/styles/square_600/public/2024-08/redpath_museum_exterior_winter_0.jpg?itok=wHVGAo61)

[Map from: Google Maps](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/styles/square_600/public/2024-08/McGill%20University.jpg?itok=o3jGBk90)

**Location:** Montreal, Canada  
**Language of instruction:** English  
**Tuition payable to:** UBC  
**Program website:** [McGill University Exchange Website](https://www.mcgill.ca/mcgillabroad/come-mcgill)  
**Terms available:** Term 1, Term 2, Full year Term 1 \+ 2 \(UBC Term 1 start\)

[Apply](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/node/3146)

## Who can go?

-   Exchange students can take coursework in most areas of study
-   Students must have a minimum cumulative average of 73% to attend this university
-   Students applying for Law must apply by the Round 1 deadline\. This is to ensure they are nominated and can register for courses at the same time as McGill Law students\. 

**When applying to Go Global:**

-   Law students: Select 'University of McGill\-LAW'
-   All other students: Select 'University of McGill\-Uniwide' 

## Academic planning

### Term dates

-   UBC Term 1 \(McGill Semester 1\): Early September to late December
-   UBC Term 2 \(McGill Semester 2\): Early January to late April
-   UBC Full Year \(McGill Semester 1 \+ 2\): Early September \- late April

### Areas of study available:

-   Arts
-   Education
-   Engineering
-   Fine Arts
-   Health Sciences
-   Land and Food Systems
-   Law
-   Science

### Course availability and restrictions

-   [Please research applicable course restrictions on the McGill University's exchange website](https://www.mcgill.ca/mcgillabroad/files/mcgillabroad/mcgill_exchange_fact_sheet_2026-2027.pdf)
-   Faculties not open to exchange students: Medicine, Dentistry, Continuing Studies
-   Schulich School of Music: strongly recommends exchange students start in the Fall term
-   School of Nursing: applicants must be from a U21 partner institution
-   Architecture, Education, Law, Music, Management and Nursing students: must already be registered in the same degree program in their home university
-   Engineering: limited spaces in Chemical, Civil and Mechanical disciplines
-   Law: There is no strict French requirement for exchange students applying to the Faculty of Law\. It is important for exchange students to know that the McGill program is a bilingual program and readings can be in either English or French and students can ask questions in either language\. Please note that it is also possible to take a French as a Second Language course at McGill as part of your exchange\.
-   Students are permitted to take up to 1 course outside their admitted faculty if space permits and there are no restrictions\. **Starting Fall 2026 onwards, students will be required to take a minimum of 60% of their courses in their admitted faculty\.**

[Partner Course Information](https://coursecatalogue.mcgill.ca/en/)

### Course equivalency Formula

-   Same as UBC credits

### Course load Information

-   Average course load: 4\-5 courses \(12\-15 credits\) per term
-   Full year is normally 30 credits

### Transfer credit

The [transfer credit process](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/transfer-credits-go-global "Transfer credits for Go Global") takes approximately 16 weeks following each submission deadline\. You should allow sufficient time to meet important deadlines that may affect you \(e\.g\. application for graduation, registration in courses that require prerequisites that you took on exchange, entry to a major/honours program, etc\.\)

[Search for previously approved courses](https://tcp.goglobal.ubc.ca/search)

## Student experience

**Housing**   
[Information on accommodation](https://www.mcgill.ca/students/housing/residence-options/exchange-students)  
   
**Accessibility**    
Some destinations may be more accessible than others for students with disability\-related accommodations\. If you identify with having a disability or pre\-existing health condition which could impact your participation, or if you require academic accommodation, please contact a Go Global advisor before applying to explore options that are best for you\.  

[**Equaldex**](https://www.equaldex.com/region/canada)    
The Equality Index measures the current status of LGBTQ\+ rights, laws, and freedoms\.  

**Social Media** 

-   [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/mcgillu/) 
    
-   [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@mcgillu) 
    
-   [LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/school/mcgill-university/?originalSubdomain=ca)
    

[**Read Student Reports**](https://goglobal.students.ubc.ca/ggoutboundapplications)

## Finances and funding

While you’re learning abroad, you remain a UBC student and are eligible for UBC awards, scholarships, and financial assistance\.   

-   15 credits or equivalent full\-time program tuition per term, paid to UBC

**Financial Planning** 

-   [Cost of Living Calculator](https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/Montreal)
-   [Budgeting for Exchange](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/budgeting-exchange-research-and-study "Budgeting for Exchange, Research and Study Abroad") \(UBCV\)
-   [Money Matters](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/global-engagement-office/go-global/outbound-exchange-program/money-matters/) \(UBCO\) 

**Awards & Scholarships**    
All awards and scholarships available through Go Global:    
[UBCV Students](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/new-programs-ubc-students/new-student-resources/awards-students-participating-go-global "Awards for students participating in Go Global")    
[UBCO Students](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/global-engagement-office/go-global/outbound-exchange-program/money-matters/#awards)

## Who can go?

-   Only COMM \(UBCV\) are eligible to apply to this partner university
    
-   Please note that students may only go for one term
    
-   There is mandatory 3 day orientation before the beginning of each term

title: Application process
content_markdown:
#### Instructions 

1.  **Complete the online application\.** After you are nominated by Tec de Monterrey, our system will send you an email prompting you to log in to the Student Application Portal and submit your online application\. After submitting, you will receive a confirmation email with your UBC student number\. \(Check your junk/spam folder for our email\!\) You will need this number for all steps in the application process, and during your time at UBC\.
2.  **Submit your application documents\.** Prepare and provide supporting application documents \(see section "Application Documents Checklist,” below\)\. Make sure that your International Programs office submits all required documents to UBC that correspond to the round you’re applying to by the deadline \(Round 1: April 1; Round 2: September 15\)
3.  **Accept your offer\.** Once Go Global has reviewed your application documents and you’ve been accepted, you will receive a link to accept your offer\. Make sure to accept your offer **once you open the link** because it expires\.  
4.  **Create a Campus\-Wide Login \(CWL\) account\.** Follow the instructions under ["Student Accounts \(CWL Account Upgrader\)"](https://it.ubc.ca/services/accounts-passwords/campus-wide-login-cwl/how-create-account) to create a UBC CWL account\. The CWL system provides access to many of the university’s online systems\. 
5.  **Complete the online housing application\.** All students in the Tec\-UBC Joint Academic Program are guaranteed on\-campus housing, but space is in high demand and students must apply by **May 1** for a September start or by **Oct\. 1** for a January start\. Rank your residence choices on the application\. While UBC makes an effort to place you in the residence of your choice, placement is based on availability\. 
    
    - **Row 1**
    
      - **Cell 1:**
      
        1.  Go to the [Student Housing and Community Services Online Service Centre](https://secure.housing.ubc.ca/) and log in under “UBC New Applicants, Students, Staff with CWL ID\.”
        2.  Log in with **SecureLink\.**
        3.  Select “Student, Applicant, External Student Portal” to request your SecureLink\.
        4.  Select “Application” and then “Apply\.”
        5.  Select the application for the year/session you are coming to UBC: e\.g\., 2025/2026 Winter Session \(25W\)\. \(Note: Select this option regardless of your study term\. We will inform the housing office whether you are coming for one or two terms because there is no place for you to indicate this on the application\.\)
        6.  Under "faculty," enter “Go Global Program, year 1\.”
        7.  There is a **$50 non\-refundable application fee**\. Pay your deposit via Visa or MasterCard only\.
        8.  If you have questions about your application and payment, [contact UBC housing directly](mailto:information@housing.ubc.ca)\.
    
6.  **Accept the housing offer and pay the housing deposit by the deadline\.** The UBC Housing office will send an offer to you by email\. The housing deposit \(about $1,000 for shared units and $1,200 for studios\) must be paid by Visa or MasterCard\.  
7.  **Register with** [**UBC’s Centre for Accessibility**](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility)**, if applicable\.** Students with disabilities and ongoing medical conditions must register with [UBC’s Centre for Accessibility](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility)\. We strongly recommend beginning this process at the same time as your application\. 

#### Application documents  

It is your responsibility to prepare and provide these documents to your International Programs office\. Tec will submit them to Go Global on your behalf by uploading them to the nomination platform before the application due date\. Please check our [key dates page](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/coming-ubc/coming-ubc-exchange/key-dates-applying-ubc-exchange "Key dates for applying to UBC on exchange") for deadlines\.   

**Checklist:** 

-   Current official academic transcript
-   Official translation of academic transcript if the original transcript is not in English\.
-   Proof of English proficiency: TOEFL score or equivalent
-   Passport copy \(biographical page only\)
-   Your [UBC Tec Joint Academic program proposed course list](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/sites/default/files/2026-01/2026-2027%20UBC%20Tec%20Study%20Abroad%20Proposed%20Course%20List.pdf)\. This list will **not** be used for registration, only for admission purposes\.
-   Additional supporting documents as needed for students planning to take courses in certain faculties or disciplines at UBC, such as courses in visual arts or music\.  

#### Study Permits and Provincial Attestation Letters

***For full\-year and split\-year students only:*** **Wait to obtain a Provincial Attestation Letter** \(PAL\)\. This document is used for initial [study permit applications](http://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/study-permits) from outside Canada\. Within two \(2\) weeks of students accepting their admission offer in the Applicant Service Centre, the PAL will be emailed directly to students\. More information about the PAL and other documents required for study permit applications can be found [here](https://students.ubc.ca/international-student-guide/immigration/study-permits/ubc-documents-required-study-permit)\.   
  
**NOTE**: Because of the limited number of PALs available, students will only receive one \(1\) PAL\. You MUST ensure all information is correct prior to accepting your admission offer\. **We are unable to re\-issue PALs** due to incorrectly submitted information \(e\.g\. wrong birthdate, misspelled name, incorrect address, etc\.\)\. If you do not require a PAL, **notify Go Global within five \(5\) business days** of the email notification about your admission\. Should you have any questions about the PAL process, contact Go Global\. For questions pertaining to study permit applications, please contact [International Student Advising](http://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/international-student-advising)\.

    ##### **Applications extended to February 28, 2025**
    
    Application instructions [here](http://global.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/global-seminars/preparing-apply)\.
    
    [Apply](http://ubc-horizons.symplicity.com/student)

##### About the course

This Go Global Seminar offers an innovative approach to knowledge diplomacy, informed by the UN’s Global Citizenship framework, to bring trans\-perspectives that advance transdisciplinary, transnational, translanguaging and transmedia approaches to 21st C learning in an experiential art as research learning opportunity\.  

In May 2025, the Bogota Museum of Modern Art \(MAMBO\) Research Center will host a collaborative week of activities involving researchers and students from The University of British Columbia \(Canada\), Helwan University \(Egypt\), and University of the Andes \(Colombia\) and key museums in Bogota\. This initiative aligns with MAMBO's mission to foster knowledge and co\-creation spaces through academic activities and artistic research workshops in partnership with international universities and local museum networks to establish public scholarship as a core competency\.  

Students will form collaborative teams for an intensive week studying public art as a pedagogic prompt through site visits to key museums in Bogota, concluding the week with a research seminar delivered to international faculty and an exhibition of work\-in\-progress\. Upon returning to UBC, students will continue to collaborate to prepare a team podcast for MAMBO Research Center, and a final team paper for publication in possible academic or student journals\. 

The course will provide a practical and real\-world environment for students to engage in research, dialogue and artistic exploration\. Key activities will include collaborative research projects, interactive workshops with artists\-in\-residence, and creative sessions aimed at developing co\-creation skills and promoting innovative approaches to art and museum studies\. This immersive experience will enrich student understandings of the role of art in society and contribute to the academic and professional discourse in education, and art education specifically\. 

##### Program eligibility  

###### **General Global Seminar requirements**

To participate in a Global Seminar, students must: 

-   Be in good standing in their faculty \(as defined by home faculty\)  
-   In the year leading up to the Global Seminar, have full\-time student status \(as defined by home faculty\)    
-   Have completed 2nd year requirements before the start of the program \(i\.e\. 3rd or 4th year standing\)  
-   Have at least a 70% academic average in your last full\-time academic session before applying    
-   Maintain a 70% academic average leading up to the program  
-   Meet any program\-specific requirements listed below including pre\-requisites before participating 

###### **Program Specific requirements**

-   This program may be of interest to: Education, Arts, Interdisciplinary majors\.
-   Minimum year level for participants: 4th year undergraduate or above, graduate students 

**Final selection will be made by the lead faculty program directors\. Space in the program may be limited\.** 

Graduating students registered full\-time \(min 9 credits in most faculties\) in Term 2 may participate in a Global Seminar as an Unclassified student in the summer\. During the selection process, preference may be given to students returning to UBC in Term 1\.

##### Experience and conditions in the Field

There are no major accessibility considerations\. The museums and the hotel are all accessible, and we will ensure that all activities are designed to accommodate students with disabilities\. 

##### Accommodations

share accommodations in hotel or hostels

##### Program fees and costs

###### **Approximate fees:** $1200\-1500\*

\*The final fee depends on the number of students in the seminar\. All Global Seminars only run if there is a minimum number of students enrolled\.  

###### **Program fees include:**

-   Accommodation  
-   Program\-related travel in\-country; \(e\.g\. buses\)  
-   Excursions and entrance fees  
-   Some group meals  
-   On\-site guest lectures

Note that students may occasionally be asked to take private or public transport to\-and\-from program activities at their own cost \(e\.g\. local buses, metros/subways, taxis/ride\-shares in urban areas\.\)

###### **Not Included:**  

-   Go Global Fee \($423\.25\)
-   Flights 
-   UBC tuition for credits   
-   Visa/country entrance fees   
-   Health or travel insurance  
-   Most meals 
-   Personal spending money\*   

\* Some examples of personal costs included: mobile communication, personal transportation that is not related to the learning outcomes of the program, additional meals that are not already identified as part of the Program Fee, immunizations, Visas, etc\.  

[Back to All Global Seminar Programs](https://goglobal.ubc.ca/go-global/programs-ubc-students/global-seminars/programs "Global Seminar Programs")

### Program Safety

All travel and program activities involve risk of harm to participants\. Go Global and Seminar program leads take reasonable precautions to reduce risks\. However, not all harms can be anticipated or prevented\. 

While travelling on UBC programs, students have a responsibility for their own safety and the safety of the group\.

Some common issues for travellers include:

-   Illness and injuries \(e\.g\. respiratory illnesses, flu, food poisoning, sprained ankles, etc\.\)
-   Fatigue and heat exhaustion
-   Violence like robbery, or gender\- and race\-based harassment or attacks, especially in urban areas
-   Traffic accidents
-   Lost documents \(passports, credit cards, etc\.\)

**Before Applying:**

-   Get to know the places you will be travelling by using available resources like [Global Affairs Canada travel reports](https://travel.gc.ca/travelling/advisories)\.
-   Consider your own mental and physical health alongside what you know about the conditions during the program \(e\.g\. how physical is the program? What are the living conditions? What can I do to prepare myself?\)

**Before departure:**  

-   Participate in all pre\-departure activities offered by Go Global and your program teaching team to learn about the program and ways to prevent and respond to incidents\.
-   Ensure you have adequate travel medical insurance that will cover you in the location and for the duration of your trip\.
-   Be aware of how to use your travel medical insurance, if you need it, and where to access medical care or other emergency assistance in the locations where you will be travelling\. 

**During the program:** 

-   If you don’t feel safe, say something\! Let your program leads know how you feel, or about incidents that occur\. Don’t hesitate to contact Go Global during your program\. 
-   Know your own needs: be aware of your own mental and physical health and your limits\. Communicate with your program lead and group about making adjustments, as needed\. 

#### **Public health: COVID\-19 and other diseases**

Students and faculty are required to comply with the entry requirements of the host country, regulations of transportation carriers, and any local public health orders\. These rules might require vaccinations \(e\.g\. for COVID\-19, yellow fever, etc\.\) to enter the country or to participate in certain program activities\. Some places may require masking, testing or isolation in various circumstances\. It is your responsibility to research and comply with any requirements\.

COVID\-19 and other infections can spread easily in a group setting\. Most programs involve shared accommodations\. Unless required by local public health authorities, isolation for those infected during the program may not be possible\.   
   
Review local requirements before applying and before departure\. Check the [Global Affairs Canada Advisory](https://travel.gc.ca/travelling/advisories) under Entry Requirements for your Global Seminar destination to learn more\. Keep in mind that program conditions can vary and rules can change before or during your trip\.

title: City University of Hong Kong - College of Science and Engineering Summer Research Exchange Programme
content_markdown:
## About the program

**Program dates:** ​Early June \- Early August

The City University of Hong Kong College of Science and Engineering Summer Research Exchange Programme is designed to give engineering and science students the opportunity to conduct scientific research related to their academic studies and expanding their horizons\. Students conduct research in an assigned topic area under the supervision of a CUHK faculty\. Additionally, student will have the opportunity to participate in outside classroom activities\. For example, industrial visits and cultural events will be organized to give them a brief introduction of the industrial establishment in Hong Kong as well as a taste of the Chinese culture\.

### Research areas:

-   Engineering
-   Science

[See Program Details](https://www.cityu.edu.hk/ceng/global-outreach/student-exchange/inbound-exchange/summer-exchange-programme)

## Eligibility requirements

### General Research Abroad eligibility

-   You must have at least a 70% average in your most recent academic term of full\-time studies prior to application\. We are looking at your Term 1 \(Fall term\) grades for summer research abroad experiences
-   Full\-time student status as defined by your faculty in the year prior to your research abroad experience
-   Be a UBC student in good standing \(e\.g\., not be under academic or non\-academic discipline\)
-   You must maintain a 70% average prior to your departure to participate in the program 

### Program\-specific requirements

-   Be a, 3rd, or 4th year student  by the time the program begins \(including students graduating in May\) in Science or Applied Science\.
-   Meet any additional lab project requirements as outlined on the program website\.

### Accessibility

If you are considering applying for a Go Global program and you identify as having a [disability](https://universitycounsel.ubc.ca/policies/disability-accommodation-policy/) or pre\-existing health condition, you are encouraged to discuss any disability\-related barriers with The Centre for Accessibility to enhance your full participation in the program\.

[The Centre for Accessibility \(Vancouver\)](https://students.ubc.ca/about-student-services/centre-for-accessibility)

[Disability Resource Centre \(Okanagan\)](https://students.ok.ubc.ca/academic-success/disability-resources)

### Transfer credit

UBC does not recognize credit for Research Abroad programs and does not grant transfer credit for these experiences\. If a partner university offers credit for your Research Abroad program, save the transcript or certificate of completion for your future records\.

## How to apply

After you submit your application to Go Global, you will be contacted by the advisor with instructions on the next steps for applying directly to your program\(s\) of choice\.

### 1\. Apply to Go Global once you’ve identified programs you're interested in

-   Submit your Go Global application [online](https://ubc-horizons.symplicity.com/student)\. You can apply for up to 3 programs on one application\.
-   Go Global will contact you with instructions on how to apply to the partner and an electronic copy of your UBC transcript\.

### 2\. Apply directly to the partner university

-   Each research program will have detailed instructions on how to apply and strict submission deadlines\.
-   All research programs will need supporting documents that typically include:
    -   Academic references \(1 – 3\)
    -   Letter of intent
    -   Curriculum vitae
    -   UBC transcript

## Application deadline

[December 10, 2025](https://ubc-horizons.symplicity.com/student)

## Housing

Students are encouraged to apply for on\-campus dormitory on the partner application\. Room preferences include single or double\. Requests will be carefully considered; however, due to limited rooms, students are not guaranteed with dormitory\. Alternatively, off\-campus housing information will be provided\.

## Program costs and fees

Students are responsible for the cost of travel and living associated with participating in this program, including program fees\.  

For more information on the cost of living in Hong Kong, please check out this [website](http://www.cityu.edu.hk/geo/ies_abouthk.htm)\.

## Go Global fee and withdrawal policy

The Go Global Fee \($431\.50\) is an administrative fee required for all applicants to all Go Global programs\. The fee will be posted to your Workday account 1\-3 weeks following your acceptance to the partner program, and will be due approximately 2 weeks later\. You will be notified of the due date by email once the fee is posted\. The fee is **non\-refundable**\. However, it may be adjusted if you withdraw from your Research Abroad experience\.

#### **If you withdraw from Go Global**

To withdraw from your Go Global Research Abroad program, you must contact Go Global to request a withdrawal\. You will then be asked to complete a short withdrawal form\.

Students who withdraw from a Go Global Research Abroad Program by March 30th will have their Go Global fee adjusted to $335\.00 \(a refund of $96\.50\)\.

If you have questions or would like to request a withdrawal, please connect with your Go Global advisor or contact Go Global [here](http://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5no0NEltKbm0yY6)\.

## Awards and funding for Research Abroad

$1,000 per research experience

### Eligibility requirements

All students accepted into a research abroad program, through Go Global, will be considered for this award\. A separate application is not required\. If you meet the eligibility criteria, then you will be notified of your award near the start of the summer term\.

To be eligible for the award, you must have an average of at least 70% on your best 24 credits in the Winter Session of the previous year \(with no failed or incomplete courses\)\. If you were on a co\-op work term, you must have at least 70% on your best 12 credits in the other term\. 

## Pre\-Departure Policy

UBC is committed to preparing students for safe and successful international experiences\. In order to achieve this, any student participating in a Go Global Program must complete the following:

-   All [UBC Student Safety Abroad](https://safetyabroad.ubc.ca/) requirements
-   Go Global Program\-specific [pre\-departure requirements](http://global.ubc.ca/go-global/international-experiences/exchange/go-global-exchange-pre-departure-program)

Failure to successfully complete these and any other requirements may result in withdrawal from the Go Global Program\.

## Contact Go Global

[SUBMIT YOUR QUESTIONS HERE](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5no0NEltKbm0yY6)

### In\-person and Virtual Drop\-in advising hours

If you need to book an advising appointment, please complete the [online request form](https://ubc.ca1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3EEmkwnTWtrG04Z)\. Appointments will be held through Zoom or by phone, and can be scheduled between **8:30 am and 4:30 pm PT** from **Monday to Friday\.** 

If you require an appointment outside of these hours, contact Go Global and they will do their best to accommodate\. Appointments outside of regular hours can only be accommodated virtually\.

\-\->

-   **Tuesday:** 1:00 \- 3:00 pm
-   **Wednesday:** 1:00 \- 3:00 pm

Go Global offers both **in\-person** and **virtual drop\-in advising** [**through Zoom**](https://ubc.zoom.us/j/63675540433?pwd=NkhtYlZYNVFSTzNoS3RDaXBYMGhzdz09) during the times listed above\.
